This stance aligns with a growing trend of companies and investors prioritizing sustainability alongside financial performance.

title: Microsoft will be carbon negative by 2030
summary: Microsoft announced an ambitious goal to become carbon negative by 2030 and by 2050, remove all carbon the company has emitted since its founding in 1975. This plan involves reducing emissions by over half by 2030, expanding its internal carbon fee to cover supply and value chains, and launching a $1 billion Climate Innovation Fund to accelerate carbon reduction and removal technologies. The company also aims to empower customers to reduce their own carbon footprints and will publish an annual Environmental Sustainability Report for transparency.

title: Microsoft Raises Stakes in Corporate Climate-Pledge Race
summary: Microsoft is stepping up its climate commitment by pledging to become "carbon negative" by 2030, meaning it will remove more carbon from the atmosphere than it produces. This commitment goes beyond those made by many of its competitors.

The program will empower researchers and organizations by providing access to technology, resources, and technical experts to accelerate medical research, gain global health insights, and improve health equity. Several initial grantees include BRAC, Fred Hutchinson Cancer Research Center, Intelligent Retinal Imaging Systems (IRIS), Novartis Foundation, PATH, and Seattle Children's Research Institute.

This initiative aims to expedite trials by enabling remote participation, document sharing, and simultaneous editing, thus addressing challenges posed by time, distance, and travel costs in traditional proceedings. The rollout targets over 40% of civil suits in district courts and is part of broader legal reforms for digitalizing and streamlining the judicial process in Japan.

Key projects include work with Seattle Children’s Research Institute on SIDS, the Novartis Foundation on leprosy elimination, and Fred Hutchinson Cancer Research Center on cancer prevention.

title: IBM CEO Ginni Rometty stepping down, cloud boss Arvind Krishna to succeed
summary: Ginni Rometty is stepping down as CEO of IBM after eight years, with cloud boss Arvind Krishna set to succeed her in April. Rometty, a 40-year IBM veteran, spearheaded numerous acquisitions, including the $34 billion Red Hat deal, as the company worked to catch up in the cloud services market. Despite a recent revenue growth, IBM's stock value declined about a quarter during her tenure, and the company's turnaround remains ongoing.

title: Google, Microsoft and the strange world of corporate greenwashing
summary: This article examines the prevalence of corporate greenwashing, especially among major companies like Google and Microsoft, who announce ambitious net-zero targets but often rely on creative accounting and carbon offsets. The piece concludes that increasing pressure from investors and activists may encourage more genuine action from corporations beyond mere pledges.

title: IITian Arvind Krishna to be new IBM CEO, replacing Ginni Rometty
summary: International Business Machines Corp. has named Arvind Krishna as its new chief executive officer, succeeding Ginni Rometty. The transition comes as IBM continues its efforts to rejuvenate and boost its cloud services business.

summary: Arvind Krishna has been named the new CEO of IBM, replacing Virginia Rometty. title: IBM replaces CEO: Ginni Rometty is on her way out
summary: IBM has named Arvind Krishna as its new chief executive officer, replacing Ginni Rometty, who will transition to executive chairman before retiring at the end of the year. Rometty, the company's first female CEO, staked IBM's future on hybrid cloud and oversaw the $34 billion Red Hat purchase, though the company's market value and revenue declined during her tenure.

It will focus on disease prevention and treatment, understanding mortality, and addressing healthcare inequities for underserved populations.

summary: Target's CIO, Michael McNamara, discusses how the company rebuilt its technology stack after a 2013 data breach to refine its digital customer experience. McNamara also touches on the challenges of creating inspiring online experiences for different product categories and the slow maturation of new technologies like RFID and autonomous vehicles.

summary: Arvind Krishna, IBM’s new CEO, is credited with conceptualizing the company’s hybrid cloud strategy in 2017, a move that revitalized the 108-year-old tech giant. His vision led to the acquisition of Red Hat and a strategic shift towards cloud computing, similar to Satya Nadella's successful leadership at Microsoft. summary: Starbucks is enhancing its customer experience through the deployment of AI-equipped hardware and analytics. These efforts, combined with significant growth in its loyalty program and digital customer base, are contributing to improved service, brand loyalty, and new offerings.

summary: Microsoft has appointed Ahmed Mazhari as its new President and Corporate Vice President for Asia, effective February 10, 2020. The company plans to use the new capital to further develop its product and strategically grow its team, rather than for a rapid sales expansion.

title: Dangerous Domain Corp.com Goes Up for Sale
summary: The domain corp.com, owned by Mike O'Connor, is being sold for $1.7 million due to its dangerous potential for namespace collisions in Windows networks. Early versions of Windows encouraged configurations that lead internal company networks to try and share sensitive data with corp.com, potentially creating a "corporate botnet" for whoever controls the domain. Security experts like Jeff Schmidt have observed massive amounts of sensitive corporate traffic being misdirected to corp.com, highlighting a long-standing security vulnerability that Microsoft has been slow to address effectively.

title: CVP Jeff Teper takes over leadership of Microsoft Teams, What does it mean for the Future?
summary: Jeff Teper, Microsoft CVP of Office apps, SharePoint, OneDrive, and Stream, has assumed leadership of Microsoft Teams. This move, following Brian MacDonald's retirement, consolidates key collaboration products under one leader, which is expected to improve integration and user experience between Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive, and Stream. The article discusses potential benefits and areas for improvement with this new leadership structure.

title: Slack clarifies IBM speculation
summary: Slack clarified speculation regarding an expanded deal with IBM after reports indicated all 350,600 IBM employees would move to its platform, causing Slack's shares to spike. Although IBM has been Slack's largest customer for years and has expanded its usage, Slack stated it was not updating its financial guidance, leading to a decline in shares in extended trading. The potential deal, estimated at $35 million by D.A. Davidson, highlights Slack's ability to scale, as the company competes with Microsoft Teams and recently added SiriusXM as a customer.

title: Wells Fargo ends forced arbitration for sexual harassment complaints
summary: Wells Fargo & Co. announced it will no longer require arbitration for employee sexual harassment complaints, making it the first major U.S. bank to do so. This change follows discussions with stakeholders including Clean Yield Asset Management, which had submitted a shareholder proposal focused on the practice. The decision is seen as a significant step in addressing misconduct in the #MeToo era, as forced arbitration has often been criticized for obscuring complaints and protecting repeat offenders.

title: Are video games a worthwhile investment?

Lala emphasizes that gaming fits into Evolve's strategy of investing in disruptive technologies that will shape the future and advises financial advisors to understand the full ecosystem of the market.

title: Rekor signs a licensing agreement with SecurePark Technologies for reselling its iP360 Software Suite
summary: Rekor, a Nasdaq company, has signed a licensing agreement with SecurePark Technologies to enable the resale of its iP360 Parking Ticket & Permit Management Software Suite. SecurePark will offer Rekor's iP360 platform as a SaaS subscription model to parking operations customers in the United States and Canada, serving various sectors including airports, schools, and hospitals. This partnership further expands Rekor's presence in the parking management software industry, providing a complete and scalable solution integrated with vehicle recognition systems.

summary: Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison is hosting a fundraiser for President Donald Trump, aligning with a shared adversary of Amazon and its CEO Jeff Bezos. This move places Ellison among a few Silicon Valley figures who have publicly supported Trump, despite potential backlash from the tech industry.

The new platform significantly enhanced developer productivity and freed up the marketing team to make rapid content changes.

summary: KPMG is acquiring the ServiceNow practice of Wirefire Creative Inc., integrating over 20 employees and Wirefire Creative co-founder Karsten Hiemstra into KPMG's Canadian operations. title: DocuSign acquires Seal Software for $188M to enhance its AI chops
summary: DocuSign is acquiring Seal Software for $188 million to bolster its AI capabilities, particularly for its contract lifecycle management (CLM) offering. Seal Software, known for its contract analytics and data extraction services, has previously received a $15 million investment from DocuSign. This acquisition aims to provide DocuSign customers with a faster and more efficient agreement process, while Seal's customers will benefit from deeper integrations within the DocuSign Agreement Cloud.

title: Video Game Industry Hits Reset in 2020
summary: The video game industry is undergoing a significant transformation in 2020, driven by the launch of next-generation consoles and the evolution of cloud and mobile gaming. While new consoles will offer improved graphics and speed, cloud gaming is poised to disrupt the traditional console model, potentially marking the beginning of the end for dedicated gaming hardware. Mobile gaming also continues to grow, attracting more spending than all other forms of gaming combined.

title: Compuware to be sold to Houston IT company
summary: BMC Software Inc. is acquiring Detroit-based computer software company Compuware Corp. from Thoma Bravo LLC. The financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed, but the deal is expected to close in the coming months. This acquisition aims to strengthen BMC's ability to improve practices that shorten the development life cycle of information technology systems, bringing together two complementary technology offerings.

title: Increasing Signs of Gender Diversity on Corporate Boards
summary: The article discusses the increasing representation of women in executive officer roles and on corporate boards in the Morningstar US Market Index, noting a significant spike since 2010. It highlights policy changes, such as those in California, as key drivers, but also points out that many women are "double dipping" on boards, while also noting an increase in first-time female directors and the role of asset managers in promoting gender diversity.

title: Connected worker platforms bring people into digital transformation
summary: The article discusses how connected worker platforms are integrating front-line industrial workers into digital transformation initiatives, bridging gaps left by traditional ERP and manufacturing systems. These platforms, offered by vendors like Parsable, SAP, Honeywell, and Oracle, utilize next-generation technologies such as IoT analytics and AI to improve worker efficiency and collaboration. Grupo Lala, a dairy production company, successfully implemented Parsable's platform to capture metadata on how procedures are performed, realize paper savings, and increase worker engagement.

title: Humanoid Robot Market Demand, Current Outlook, Future Growth,
summary: The humanoid robot market is experiencing significant growth driven by increasing adoption in retail, education, research, and caregiving, as well as technological advancements. Software is expected to dominate the market due to the integration of AI algorithms, while biped motion types also hold a significant share. North America currently leads the market, but the Asia-Pacific region is projected to show the fastest growth.

title: Dividend Growth Investing Made Easy with ETFs
summary: This article, a guest post by Tom of Dividends Diversify, explains how dividend growth investing can be made easy through the use of Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs). It highlights the benefits of diversification offered by ETFs and discusses several popular dividend ETFs such as VYM, VIG, VYMI, and NOBL, outlining their characteristics and investment strategies. The article also touches on considerations for Canadian investors regarding withholding taxes and briefly mentions individual stock holdings.

title: Theme Lab: A Look Inside An Amazon Fulfillment Center
summary: This article details a "Theme Lab" visit to an Amazon Fulfillment Center, showcasing how robotics, IoT, AI, and human labor collaborate in the Stowing, Picking, Packing, and Shipping phases. It highlights the critical synergistic roles of these technologies and human expertise in achieving efficiency in e-commerce fulfillment. The article concludes by discussing related ETFs that track these disruptive technologies.

title: Technology trumps consumer staples in the hunt for quality
summary: This article argues that the traditional strength of consumer staples has waned, while the technology sector now offers superior investment opportunities, particularly when viewed through a "franchise power/growth framework." It highlights the shift in leadership from consumer staples to IT, attributing technology's rise to strong business franchises, network effects, and a move towards subscription-based software models. The author also compares the portfolio weightings and performance of various quality investment funds, showing a trend towards higher tech exposure.

title: Costco supply chain struggles to keep up with demand amid COVID-19 preparations
summary: Costco's supply chain faced significant challenges keeping up with surging demand as members stocked up on supplies in preparation for COVID-19. Empty shelves were observed in stores, including bread sections, as customers rushed to purchase goods. This article highlights the immediate impact of coronavirus fears on consumer buying habits and retailer operations.

title: NetApp sinks claws into Talon Storage
summary: NetApp has acquired Talon Storage, a company specializing in caching software that connects branch offices to public cloud file servers. The acquisition aims to provide a unified footprint for unstructured data, enabling seamless access for users regardless of their geographical location. Talon's FAST software will allow NetApp to offer an indirect remote office/branch office (ROBO) presence without requiring on-premises NetApp filers.

title: 7 Amplify Dashboard Tips For Working Smarter (Not Harder!)
summary: This article provides seven tips for Outbrain Amplify dashboard users to work more efficiently, including exporting data to Excel for analysis, mixing and matching new imagery for creative refreshes, and utilizing filters for performance review. It also covers bulk updating campaigns, duplicating campaigns for new ones, maintaining consistent campaign naming conventions, and customizing dashboard columns for quick performance overviews. The tips aim to save time and streamline workflows for marketing professionals using the Outbrain platform.

title: Starbucks stores may go drive-thru only or limit seating to address coronavirus concerns
summary: Starbucks announced that some of its stores in the U.S. and Canada might transition to drive-thru only or limit seating to address concerns about the coronavirus pandemic. The company plans to make these decisions on a store-by-store basis and may temporarily close stores as a last resort. Starbucks has also expanded catastrophe pay for employees affected by the virus, and its shares have significantly dropped amid the outbreak.

title: Meet Grace: Digital skills teacher, refugee advocate, dreamer
summary: Grace Nshimiyumukiza, a refugee in Kakuma camp, Kenya, taught herself computer skills and now teaches other women in the camp as a Digital Skills Trainer for the Connected Education program, a joint initiative by UNHCR and Microsoft Tech for Social Impact. Her goal is to empower youth and women to become independent by providing them with digital literacy and livelihood opportunities. Grace's work is transforming lives and challenging the narrative surrounding refugees, demonstrating their potential when given opportunities.

title: Microsoft announces change to its board of directors
summary: Microsoft Corporation announced that Co-Founder and Technology Advisor Bill Gates stepped down from its Board of Directors to focus on philanthropic priorities. He will continue to serve as a Technology Advisor to CEO Satya Nadella and other leaders. The board will now consist of 12 members.

title: Connect Analog devices to Microsoft Teams with Ribbon and AudioCodes
summary: This article discusses how to connect analog devices to Microsoft Teams using Session Border Controllers (SBCs)/Gateways from Ribbon and AudioCodes, building on past practices with Lync and Skype for Business. It highlights the use cases for analog devices and notes that while Microsoft Teams now certifies SBCs for this purpose, there is no direct "contact object" for analog devices, requiring manual dialing by Teams users. The author contrasts this with Skype for Business Server's "analog device" feature and points out that connection is primarily achieved via dialing numbers and voice routes between Teams and the SBC.

title: Bill Gates steps down from Microsoft board
summary: Bill Gates announced he is stepping down from the boards of Microsoft and Berkshire Hathaway to dedicate more time to philanthropy, focusing on global health, education, and climate change through the Gates Foundation. He will continue to serve as a technology advisor to Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella. Gates, who co-founded Microsoft in 1975, remains one of the world's richest individuals.

title: A Tribute to Amory Houghton
summary: This article is a tribute to former Congressman Amory Houghton Jr. (R-NY), who passed away at age 93. It highlights his career as CEO of Corning Glass Works and his nine terms in Congress, emphasizing his role as an exemplary moderate Republican rooted in the company and community of Corning, New York. The piece details his moderate political views, fiscal conservatism, belief in science and long-term thinking, and efforts to bridge political divides, contrasting him with the increasingly polarized political landscape, even as he remained optimistic about a moderate Republican revival.

title: Key Takeaways: The 2020 Gartner Market Guide for Network Performance Monitoring and Diagnostics
summary: This article highlights key takeaways from the 2020 Gartner Market Guide for Network Performance Monitoring and Diagnostics (NPMD), outlining Gartner's definition of the market and the impact of new dynamic network architectures. It discusses how hybrid environments, the alignment of network and security operations, and major shifts like cloud migration and increasing virtualization are affecting NPMD tools and buyer decisions. Gartner predicts that 50% of network operations teams will rearchitect their monitoring stack by 2024 due to hybrid networking and lists notable network monitoring tool providers.

title: Coronavirus Forces $600 Billion Higher Education Industry Online
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic is forcing the $600 billion higher education industry online as campuses shutter. Universities are scrambling to shift to distance learning, with professors like Analisa Packham at Vanderbilt University quickly adapting to new technologies for teaching and holding virtual office hours. This abrupt transition highlights the challenges and rapid adjustments required for both educators and students in the new remote learning environment.

title: Adaptive Biotechnologies and Microsoft expand partnership to decode COVID-19 immune response and provide open data access
summary: Adaptive Biotechnologies and Microsoft are expanding their partnership to study the immune response to COVID-19, aiming to improve detection, treatment, and prevention of the disease. They will collect de-identified blood samples and use Microsoft's machine learning and Azure cloud platform to make immune response data freely available to researchers globally. This initiative seeks to decode the immune system's response for a better understanding of COVID-19 at a population level.

title: Connected Enterprise Market to Eyewitness Massive Growth
summary: A new market study by Advance Market Analytics predicts massive growth for the Global Connected Enterprise Market by 2025. The report highlights key market drivers such as technological advancements and the adoption of IoT and AI, as well as restraints like high deployment costs and lack of uniform IoT standards. Major players in the market include Rockwell Automation, Cisco Systems, IBM, and Microsoft.

title: Hacker allegedly steals AMD Navi 21 and Xbox Series X GPU test files, demands $100 million
summary: A hacker allegedly stole test files for AMD's Navi 21 GPU and the Xbox Series X's Arden GPU, demanding $100 million to prevent a full leak. AMD confirmed a "subset" of test files were compromised but stated they are not critical to product competitiveness or security, adding that authorities are investigating the incident. The hack highlights potential security vulnerabilities at AMD.

title: CMU, C3.ai, Microsoft, and Five Leading Research Universities Launch C3.ai Digital Transformation Institute
summary: Carnegie Mellon University, alongside C3.ai, Microsoft, and five other leading research universities, has launched the C3.ai Digital Transformation Institute (C3.ai DTI). This consortium aims to accelerate the application of artificial intelligence for digital transformation across business, government, and society. The Institute's first call for research proposals will focus on using AI techniques to mitigate the spread of COVID-19 and address future pandemics.

title: Microsoft Edge is becoming the browser you didn’t know you needed
summary: Microsoft Edge is introducing several compelling new features like Collections, Immersive Reader, and vertical tabs, aiming to elevate its status beyond just a functional default browser. While some features are still in preview, they offer significant enhancements for organization, readability, and user interface. Additionally, Edge gains exclusive 4K Netflix streaming support on Windows 10 and improved privacy tools.

title: Microsoft Files Patent For Crypto Mining Linked To Body Activity Data
summary: Microsoft Technology Licensing, LLC has filed a patent for a cryptocurrency system that uses human body activity data, such as body radiation, fluid flow, brain waves, pulse rate, or heat radiation, to mine cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin. The system involves a server providing tasks to a user's device, which senses body activity, generates data, and awards cryptocurrency if the data satisfies set conditions. This innovative approach aims to verify human participation and utilize biological processes for digital currency mining.

title: Shifting Some Employees to Remote Work Permanently
summary: A Gartner survey of 317 CFOs and Finance leaders revealed that 74% plan to permanently shift at least 5% of their previously on-site workforce to remote positions post-COVID-19. This move is driven by an opportunity to realize cost benefits and minimize disruptions. Many CFOs also anticipate minimal disruption to finance operations due to increased viability of remote work for various positions.

title: Dev kits support Azure RTOS
summary: Leading microprocessor and microcontroller manufacturers like Renesas, NXP, Microchip, Qualcomm, and STMicroelectronics are expanding their support for Microsoft Azure RTOS. This initiative aims to simplify integration and development between their chips and the Azure RTOS, providing embedded developers with access to real-time performance for resource-constrained devices and integration with Azure IoT. Microsoft plans to release the full source code for all Azure RTOS components on GitHub to further facilitate development and adaptation.

title: Microsoft Buys Corp.com So Bad Guys Can’t
summary: Microsoft has purchased the domain corp.com, 26 years after its initial acquisition by Mike O’Connor, to prevent malicious actors from exploiting a namespace collision vulnerability in older Windows systems. This issue caused hundreds of thousands of corporate Windows PCs to attempt to share sensitive data with corp.com, particularly when outside the corporate network. Microsoft’s acquisition aims to protect its customers from potential data interception and reduce security risks stemming from its own Active Directory design flaws.

title: Microsoft buys Corp.com domain name, likely for seven figures
summary: Microsoft has acquired the domain name Corp.com for an undisclosed price, following the owner's intention to auction it starting at $1.7 million. The acquisition addresses "name collision" issues where Windows computers mistakenly sent traffic to Corp.com, making it a strategic security investment for Microsoft. This purchase will also provide Microsoft with valuable data to better understand and mitigate future name collision problems.

title: Microsoft buys corp.com to prevent Windows account hijacking
summary: Microsoft has purchased the Corp.com domain to prevent malicious actors from using it to steal Windows credentials or serve malicious files. This acquisition addresses a long-standing "DNS name collision" issue where Windows networks configured with "CORP" as their Active Directory domain could mistakenly try to connect to the public corp.com domain. The purchase aims to protect customers, though Microsoft advises companies to own any domain used for Active Directory to prevent future collision risks.

title: BlackBerry uncovers hacker tools that it says opened data servers for a decade
summary: BlackBerry has released a report detailing how five separate groups linked to the Chinese government have been targeting Linux systems for a decade. These hackers have used novel techniques, including disguising malicious tools as advertising software, to exfiltrate vast amounts of data from servers. The report highlights a significant blind spot in cybersecurity, as Linux powers critical global infrastructure like stock exchanges and major cloud services.

title: SPXL vs. UPRO: Head-To-Head ETF Comparison
summary: This article provides a head-to-head comparison of two leveraged S&P 500 ETFs, SPXL and UPRO, detailing their fees, performance, holdings, and ESG scores. It offers a comprehensive overview for investors to make informed decisions by comparing various metrics from expense ratios and AUM to technical indicators and analyst takes. Both ETFs offer 3x daily long leverage to the S&P 500 Index, making them tools for investors with a bullish short-term outlook on U.S. large cap stocks.

title: ETF News, Trends, Analysis, Opinions
summary: The article analyzes how thematic ETFs, particularly in cloud computing and biotech, have performed during the coronavirus turmoil, with some sub-sectors outperforming the market. It discusses the long-term viability of thematic ETFs, citing Morningstar data on their survival rates and performance against benchmarks, and highlights risks for investors. Despite recent outperformance, historical data suggests caution regarding their long-term success and emphasizes the challenges of selecting successful themes and funds.

title: PTC Launches Creo 7.0 with Powerful Enhancements for Generative Design and Simulation-Driven Design
summary: PTC has launched Creo 7.0, the latest version of its 3D CAD software, featuring powerful enhancements for generative design and simulation-driven design. This new release incorporates AI capabilities, such as Frustum generative design technology and an enhanced Ansys-powered Creo Simulation Live with real-time fluid-flow analysis, to enable designers to create optimized products faster. Creo 7.0 also introduces multibody design and improved additive manufacturing capabilities, furthering PTC's commitment to delivering innovative technology.

title: Qualys VMDR® - Vulnerability Management, Detection and Response - Now Shipping
summary: Qualys, Inc. announced the immediate availability of its VMDR® – Vulnerability Management, Detection and Response solution, which integrates critical security functions into one platform. The article includes testimonials from early adopters like Toyota Financial Services and Armor, highlighting VMDR's ability to improve vulnerability management and provide real-time, actionable remediation. Qualys also addressed a marketing campaign launched by Rapid7 against VMDR, inviting the public to a rebuttal event.

title: Zscaler wants to provide security for the cloud and mobile era
summary: Zscaler is positioning itself as a leader in SASE architecture by offering a comprehensive platform that secures traffic between endpoints and applications, leveraging its cloud-first approach. The company emphasizes its long-standing mission to provide cloud security, adapting to the fragmented application landscape and diverse user locations. Zscaler differentiates itself by consolidating more than ten traditional security and network services into one consistent cloud security platform, while also collaborating with technology partners for specialized functionalities.

title: Activist investor Starboard, which has track record of big returns in tech, finds its next target
summary: Activist investor Starboard Value is targeting business software company Commvault Systems (CVLT) by nominating four directors to its board. Starboard aims to improve Commvault's profitability and capital allocation strategy, highlighting issues with its go-to-market strategy, sales efficiency, and the speculative acquisition of Hedvig. Starboard has a strong track record of generating significant returns, particularly in technology companies, through operational activism and board refreshment.

title: Large Cap Tech Stocks Continue to Throw Their Weight Around
summary: Large-cap tech stocks, particularly those in the Nasdaq 100, are demonstrating resilience and leading recovery efforts in capital markets amidst the coronavirus pandemic. Companies like Amazon and Microsoft are driving this trend, with the Nasdaq 100 showing a 1% year-to-date gain compared to the S&P 500's 11% decline. Investors can gain exposure through ETFs like FTEC, XLK, and RWLS, which offers a large-cap over small-cap strategy.

title: AMD (NASDAQ:AMD) Reports 41% Year-Over-Year Revenue Growth, Record Notebook Sales
summary: AMD reported Q1 FY2020 earnings with $1.79 billion in revenue, marking a 41% year-over-year growth, despite missing Wall Street analyst expectations and its own previous guidance. The company saw strong performance in Ryzen and EPYC processors and record notebook sales, although overall sequential revenue dropped. AMD remains optimistic about Q2 FY2020, forecasting 21% year-over-year revenue growth.

title: What’s Changed: 2020 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Application Performance Monitoring
summary: This article highlights the key changes in the 2020 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Application Performance Monitoring, providing analysis of the latest report. It discusses the movements of vendors across the Leaders, Challengers, Visionaries, and Niche Players quadrants, detailing significant acquisitions, product integrations, and strategic focuses for companies like Cisco, Dynatrace, New Relic, Microsoft, Splunk, and Datadog. The report identifies 15 providers and offers insights into the evolving APM landscape.

title: Coca-Cola taps Microsoft for 5-year multicloud, software deal
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has signed a five-year deal with Microsoft for its software and cloud products to enhance data insights, replace fragmented systems, and facilitate remote work for its 86,000 employees. This move aims to boost efficiency amidst a challenging economic forecast and the widespread shift to remote work due to the pandemic. The deal includes Microsoft Azure, Dynamics 365, Microsoft 365, Power Platform, and Microsoft Teams.

title: Microsoft pivots to digital selling with Dynamics 365 to reach more customers
summary: Microsoft has transformed its sales model by pivoting to digital selling with Dynamics 365, enabling its more than 2,500 digital sellers to engage with customers remotely and scale for increased demand. By leveraging Dynamics 365 Sales and Sales Insights, Microsoft has boosted revenues for this segment, cut sales costs by 10 percent, and provided a personalized experience to customers, even adapting effectively during the COVID-19 pandemic. The AI-powered features, including sales accelerator and conversation intelligence, enhance seller productivity, prioritize leads, and provide actionable insights for building stronger customer relationships.

title: Five9 Inc (FIVN) Q1 2020 Earnings Call Transcript
summary: This is a transcript of Five9 Inc's Q1 2020 Earnings Call, where executives discuss financial results, the impact of COVID-19 on their business model, and strategic initiatives such as channel expansion and partnerships with AT&T Business and Zoom. The company reported record Q1 revenue and strong enterprise subscription growth, while also outlining a cautious stance for second-half guidance due to macroeconomic uncertainties. Discussions highlighted the acceleration of cloud adoption and the increasing importance of work-from-home capabilities for contact centers.

title: C3 AI Accelerates AI Application Development on AWS by 26X
summary: This report details how the C3 AI Platform significantly reduces the complexity and time required to develop enterprise AI applications on AWS, accelerating development by a factor of 26x. It compares using only AWS native services versus incorporating the C3 AI Platform, highlighting the platform's ability to simplify infrastructure provisioning and reduce coding needs. The report, written by an independent system integrator, showcases the C3 AI Platform's effectiveness in increasing developer productivity and speeding up deployment.

title: Arista Extends Open Cloud Networking Software Leadership
summary: Arista Networks has strengthened its commitment to open network software by introducing Arista switches Powered by SONiC, allowing customers to deploy SONiC software on Arista switching platforms. This initiative, enabled by a new Arista SAI offering, expands choices for enterprise datacenters and leverages Arista's hardware and support with open-source software benefits. The company is actively collaborating with Microsoft on open cloud networking, emphasizing resilience, automation, and analytics.

title: HP’s Innovative Cloud-Based Devices Enable Productivity Anytime, Anywhere
summary: HP announced new cloud-based devices, including Chromebooks and thin client solutions, designed to empower remote workers and address the security challenges of the "work from home" era. The new portfolio emphasizes sustainability, security, and performance, featuring products like the HP Elite c1030 Chromebook Enterprise with an integrated privacy screen and ocean-bound plastics. These innovations aim to provide businesses with secure, scalable, and easy-to-deploy tools for a cloud-centric workforce.

title: Halliburton lays off 1,000 employees from corporate headquarters in Houston
summary: Halliburton announced it is laying off approximately 1,000 employees from its Houston corporate headquarters due to the dramatic business downturn caused by the coronavirus pandemic and an unprecedented commodity price decline. This comes after the company closed two other Texas facilities, with some employees relocated. The article also provides a stock market update indicating a general market dip despite tech stock gains and reports on severe job losses.

title: Staying a move ahead: CEO Alan Trefler positions Pegasystems for the long game in customer engagement
summary: Pegasystems CEO Alan Trefler discusses how the company has adapted and reinvented itself five times over the years, mirroring his chess philosophy of thinking several moves ahead. The article highlights Pegasystems' focus on AI-driven customer engagement, its approach to empathy in automation, and its successful navigation of the robotic process automation (RPA) market, leading to a 25% revenue increase in the first quarter of 2020. Trefler emphasizes the increasing need for digital infrastructure changes post-COVID-19, benefiting platforms like Pegasystems.

title: EA SPORTS Announces Madden NFL 21 Will Be Available on Xbox Series X
summary: Electronic Arts announced that Madden NFL 21 will be available on Xbox Series X, with a free upgrade path for players who purchase the game on Xbox One. This ensures players won't need to buy the game twice when transitioning to the next-generation console, with specific deadlines for the upgrade offer. The announcement was made during an episode of Inside Xbox by Super Bowl MVP Patrick Mahomes.

title: Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt Cut Last Ties With The Company: Report
summary: Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt officially severed all ties with Alphabet Inc. in February 2020, ending his 19-year tenure with the company. Schmidt, who had served in various executive roles since 2001, stepped down as a technology advisor, a move that coincided with his increased involvement in government roles. His departure also came amid criticism over his dual role as an advisor to the Pentagon while Alphabet competed for the JEDI contract.

title: NetApp Hires Former Microsoft Exec Cesar Cernuda As New President
summary: NetApp announced the hiring of Cesar Cernuda, former president of Microsoft Latin America, as its new company president, effective July 1. Cernuda, who spent 23 years at Microsoft, will report to NetApp CEO and President George Kurian and focus on evolving NetApp's go-to-market strategy for cloud business opportunities. His appointment comes as NetApp is transforming from an on-premises storage focus to a seamless hybrid cloud and public cloud storage architecture.

title: The Woodruff Arts Center names Douglas Hertz as new chair of board of trustees
summary: The Woodruff Arts Center has appointed Douglas Hertz as the new chairman of its board of trustees for a one-year term starting June 1st. Hertz, who previously chaired the board from 2014 to 2017, will succeed Phil Jacobs. The center also announced several new trustees, emphasizing their commitment to the arts during uncertain times.

title: Nvidia Unveils New Data Center Chips to Speed Pace of AI
summary: Nvidia Corp. announced new Ampere graphics chips and computers for AI processing in data centers, claiming a 20x performance increase over predecessors. These new chips are designed to handle both AI training and inference tasks, a capability that will bolster Nvidia's leadership in the growing AI market. The company is selling Ampere-based computers called DGX for $199,000 each, touting their superior performance compared to traditional Intel-based server arrays.

title: Juniper Networks CEO: ‘The Goal Now Is A Self-Driving Network’
summary: Juniper Networks CEO Rami Rahim states that the company's goal is a "self-driving network," where AI takes center stage in enterprise networking. Leveraging its 2019 acquisition of Mist Systems, Juniper is injecting AI into both wired and wireless LANs through Mist’s AI engine, Marvis, to reduce human intervention and improve network efficiency. The company also aims to create an AI-driven channel experience, integrating AI into its partner portal to enhance partner support and sales cycles.

title: NetApp Appoints Former Microsoft Asia Exec Cesar Cernuda President
summary: NetApp has appointed Cesar Cernuda, former President of Microsoft Latin America and Asia Pacific, as its new President, effective July. Cernuda will lead global go-to-market operations, reporting to CEO George Kurian. His experience in transforming large global organizations is expected to accelerate NetApp's cloud and software strategy and strengthen its leadership in cloud data services.

title: Amazon Stock Benefits If AWS Is Spun Off
summary: This article discusses the potential benefits for Amazon stock if its Amazon Web Services (AWS) cloud business were spun off. The author suggests that AWS, with its faster-growing revenue and better margins compared to Amazon's e-commerce operations, could be worth more as a separate entity. The article also touches upon increasing government scrutiny on large tech companies like Amazon, Google, and Facebook regarding their dominance and potential monopolistic practices.

title: Microsoft Corp. to Expand Presence in Atlanta
summary: Microsoft Corp. is expanding its presence in Atlanta with a new facility anticipated to open in summer 2021, representing a $75 million investment and creating 1,500 new high-tech jobs in West Midtown. The new client-facing workplace will focus on artificial intelligence and cloud services, occupying 523,000 square feet in the Atlantic Yards complex. This expansion highlights Atlanta's appeal for tech growth due to its skilled workforce, innovation-friendly environment, and strong educational pipelines.

title: UnitedHealth, Microsoft build app to guard their offices from Covid-19 (and maybe yours, too)
summary: UnitedHealth and Microsoft have partnered to develop an app called ProtectWell aimed at screening employees for COVID-19 symptoms or exposure. The app utilizes UnitedHealth's clinical and data analytics capabilities along with Microsoft's AI-powered healthcare bot. It is designed to help companies reopen their offices safely during the pandemic.

title: KeyBank to incorporate Kubernetes into digital transformation strategy
summary: KeyBank announced its plan to integrate Kubernetes technology into its data center operations to further its digital transformation efforts. This move, leveraging Google Cloud's Cloud Services Platform, aims to launch new features more quickly, efficiently, and securely for its customers. KeyBank anticipates that this will enhance velocity, reliability, and governance at scale for its banking services.

title: FedEx and Microsoft join forces to transform commerce
summary: FedEx Corp. and Microsoft Corp. announced a new multiyear collaboration to transform commerce by combining FedEx's global digital and logistics network with Microsoft’s intelligent cloud services like Azure and Dynamics 365. Their first joint offering, FedEx Surround, aims to enhance supply chain visibility with near-real-time analytics, helping businesses with precise logistics and inventory management, especially for time-sensitive deliveries. This partnership seeks to reinvent commerce experiences and enable businesses to better compete in the digital landscape.

title: Coca-Cola: solving business challenges with technology
summary: This article discusses how The Coca-Cola Company (TCCC) leverages technology to address business challenges, focusing on its digital transformation program 'Digitizing for Growth'. Damiano Marabelli, Central & Eastern Europe Business Unit CIO, details IT's role in consumer and customer engagement, enterprise digitalization, and collaborations with bottling partners to enhance revenue growth management and consumer-facing applications. The company emphasizes a shift in IT's role from technology builders to architects of possibility, integrating technology into all aspects of the business to support its 'Total Beverage' strategy.

title: Sony Semiconductor Solutions and Microsoft partner to create smart camera solutions for enterprise customers
summary: Sony Semiconductor Solutions and Microsoft are partnering to create AI-powered smart camera and video analytics solutions for enterprise customers. The collaboration involves embedding Microsoft Azure AI capabilities on Sony’s intelligent vision sensor IMX500 and developing a smart camera managed app powered by Azure IoT and Cognitive Services. This initiative aims to simplify access to computer vision solutions, streamline operations, and uncover new revenue opportunities across various industries.

title: Congratulations to our 2020 Health Innovation Award winners
summary: Microsoft announced the winners of its 2020 Health Innovation Awards, recognizing customers and partners who have deployed solutions to improve healthcare experiences, insights, and care. The awards span various categories including Artificial Intelligence, Empowering Care Teams, Personalized Care, Reimagine Healthcare, Improve Operational Outcomes, and Protect Health Information. These innovations showcase how technology is being used to address critical challenges in the health industry, from reducing patient falls and enhancing clinical efficiency to managing genetic data and improving patient recruitment for clinical trials.

title: Experience modern teamwork without boundaries with the all-new Surface Hub 2S
summary: Microsoft announced the availability of Surface Hub 2S in India, an all-in-one digital whiteboard, meeting platform, and collaborative computing device designed for the modern workplace. Priced at INR 11,89,999, it aims to foster active teamwork by blending into any workspace, supporting both in-person and virtual collaboration, and enhancing productivity through seamless integration with Microsoft services like Windows 10, Microsoft Teams, and Office 365. The device, along with the Steelcase Roam mobile stand, offers flexibility and encourages dynamic interaction for creative work.

title: Tech Moves: Qualtrics exec moves to Google; NHL Seattle expands team; former Amazon exec named Bluecrew CEO; and more
summary: This article details various "Tech Moves" in the Pacific Northwest, highlighting significant personnel changes across several companies. Key appointments include a former Qualtrics EVP joining Google, an ex-Amazon executive becoming CEO of Bluecrew, and new hires for the Seattle Center Arena project and NHL Seattle. Other notable moves include board appointments, new CROs, and executive leadership roles in marketing, finance, and engineering across the tech industry.

title: Microsoft Teams Up with OpenAI to Build Huge AI Supercomputer in Azure
summary: Microsoft has partnered with OpenAI to develop one of the world's fastest AI supercomputers, leveraging Azure's infrastructure. This supercomputer boasts significant processing power, including 285,000 core machine power and 10,000 GPUs, funded by OpenAI with contributions from Microsoft. The collaboration aims to advance AI development for the benefit of humanity, rather than financial returns, and builds on OpenAI's deep learning approach.

title: FedEx, Microsoft Join Forces Against Amazon for Package Shipping
summary: FedEx Corp. and Microsoft Corp. are collaborating to offer commercial shipping customers early warnings about potential delays due to weather, traffic, and other issues, directly competing with Amazon.com Inc. This new service, called FedEx Surround, will leverage Microsoft's cloud software and AI tools to provide real-time data to improve package movement, especially for high-priority shipments. The partnership aims to provide commercial customers with logistics tools that can serve as an alternative to Amazon for both small and large retailers.

title: Manhattan Associates Announces Cloud-Native WMS
summary: Manhattan Associates has launched Manhattan Active Warehouse Management (WM), the world's first cloud-native, enterprise-class WMS. This new solution is built entirely from microservices, offering enhanced speed, adaptability, and ease of use in distribution management. It features modern mobile experiences, automatic scaling, embedded machine learning, and gamification theory to improve employee productivity.

title: Different Market, Same Leaders: Tech ETFs Thrive In Pandemic
summary: In April 2020, even amidst market volatility and the COVID-19 pandemic, technology-focused ETFs led the recovery, echoing previous market trends. Direxion's leveraged tech ETFs, such as TECL, SOXL, and WEBL, showed significant gains, driven by strong performances in financial technology, semiconductor industries, and companies benefiting from increased online activity. This indicates a market belief that technology will continue to spearhead economic recovery despite overall uncertainty.

title: Microsoft Teams Policy-based compliance recording API is now Generally Available
summary: The Microsoft Teams updateRecordingStatus API, which enables policy/compliance-based session recording, is now generally available. This API allows recordings of calls and meetings to meet regulatory requirements, capturing audio, video, and screen sharing across all Microsoft Teams endpoints. An additional Microsoft license will be required for its use, and certified partners offer solutions to capture these recordings.

title: Hewlett Packard Enterprise plans cuts in jobs, executive pay to temper sales slump
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) announced plans to cut costs by US$1 billion by the end of fiscal 2022, including job cuts and executive pay reductions, following a decline in sales due to the coronavirus pandemic. The company reported a 16% revenue drop to US$6 billion in the recent quarter and is implementing measures like simplifying its product portfolio and consolidating offices to recover from supply chain disruptions. CEO Antonio Neri expects sales to recover sequentially but acknowledges the uncertainty of the economic downturn.

title: Expedia Group CEO Peter Kern: 'Google's a problem for everyone who sells something online'
summary: Expedia Group CEO Peter Kern criticized Google for its dual role as a competitor and a major source of customer traffic, stating it's an issue for all online sellers. Kern indicated a shift in strategy for Expedia to reduce its reliance on Google and performance marketing by improving internal merchandising and customer understanding. These comments follow Expedia's quarterly earnings report where marketing expenses dropped significantly, and the company reported a major reduction in business due to COVID-19.

title: Same Old Leadership Song Lifts These Leveraged ETFs
summary: Technology sector leadership is driving the stock market's recovery from March lows, benefiting leveraged ETFs like Direxion Daily Technology Bull 3X Shares (NYSE: TECL) and Direxion Daily Dow Jones Internet Bull 3X Shares (NYSE: WEBL). TECL is a triple-leveraged play on Microsoft and Apple, while WEBL offers a similar leveraged exposure to internet giants like Amazon, Facebook, and Netflix. Both ETFs have seen significant gains and investor interest due to the strong performance of their underlying tech and internet components.

title: Software piracy: HC awards Rs 30 lakh damages to software giants Microsoft, Adobe
summary: The Delhi High Court has awarded Rs 30 lakh in damages to Microsoft Corporation, Adobe Systems, and Quest Software, restraining a Delhi-based company, Chetu, from using or distributing their pirated software. The court's decision came after an investigation revealed Chetu was using unlicensed software despite claiming to be a Microsoft certified partner. The awarded damages are to be equally shared among the three software giants.

title: Kennametal backs its smart factories with SAP on Azure
summary: Kennametal, a global leader in advanced materials and tooling, successfully migrated its 3-terabyte SAP ERP system to Microsoft Azure over a single weekend. This move significantly improved security, application performance, and data accessibility, fueling their digital transformation towards smart factories. The cloud-based architecture also enhanced business continuity and disaster recovery capabilities, allowing Kennametal to explore new opportunities in machine learning and AI.

title: SB Technology holds Japan’s first earnings briefing on Microsoft Teams
summary: SB Technology Corporation successfully held Japan's first earnings results briefing for over 80 attendees using Microsoft Teams, marking a significant shift to virtual business events amidst the COVID-19 pandemic. The company meticulously prepared for the online briefing by providing user manuals, conducting connection tests, and ensuring social distancing measures for the presenters. This successful event serves as a best practice for other Japanese companies looking to conduct secure and efficient virtual communications.

title: Pega Introduces Pega Process Fabric - The "Platform for Platforms" That Streamlines Work Across Enterprise Siloes
summary: Pegasystems Inc. (NASDAQ: PEGA) announced Pega Process Fabric™, a new cloud-based software architecture designed to streamline work across distributed enterprise technologies. This "platform for platforms" unifies work across the enterprise by breaking down technology silos, improving user experiences for employees, customers, and partners. It achieves this by combining dynamic APIs, an open UX framework, UI components, robotic automation, and data virtualization, allowing disparate systems to act as one cohesive whole.

title: Cisco Moves ACI Strategy Forward
summary: Cisco is advancing its hybrid cloud computing strategy with the release of version 5.0 of its Application Centric Infrastructure (ACI), adding support for AWS transit gateways and enhanced integration with Microsoft Azure and Kubernetes. This update aims to provide a centralized view of cloud resources and simplify configurations, offering IT teams networking services equivalent to those historically provided on-premises. The strategy emphasizes hybrid cloud management and automation, making networking services more accessible via APIs and GUIs, and fostering greater collaboration between NetOps and DevOps.

title: Nanox, maker of a low-cost scanning service to replace X-rays, expands Series B to $51M
summary: Nanox, an Israeli startup developing a low-cost, small-scale scanning system that offers "medical screening as a service" to replace traditional, expensive imaging machines, has expanded its Series B funding round to $51 million. This expansion includes a $20 million investment from South Korean carrier SK Telecom, which plans to distribute Nanox scanners and resell its pay-per-scan imaging service, Nanox.Cloud. The company aims to make early detection scans more accessible globally, particularly for conditions like cancer, by distributing 15,000 machines over the coming years.

title: Amdocs transforms its own culture to help service providers move to the cloud
summary: Amdocs undertook a significant cultural and technological transformation, leveraging TM Forum's Open Digital Framework, to enable its customers to adopt cloud services faster. This involved shifting its portfolio to a cloud-native, microservices-based architecture, upskilling over 10,000 employees in DevOps, and increasing R&D velocity by over 50%. The successful internal transformation is now delivering tangible benefits for Amdocs' customers, such as Sprint, by speeding up time to market for new services and reducing operational costs.

title: US Cloud Data Firm NetApp To Acquire Israel’s Spot.io
summary: US cloud data services company NetApp is set to acquire the US-Israeli company Spot.io for an estimated $450 million. Spot.io helps businesses manage cloud workloads and slash computing costs for clients like Moovit, Ticketmaster, and Wix. This acquisition aims to establish NetApp's leadership in cloud management and infrastructure tools, promising significant cost savings for customers by combining their technologies into an Application Driven Infrastructure.

title: How Snowflake is challenging the cloud-native database giants
summary: This article examines how Snowflake Inc. is competing with major cloud providers like Amazon Web Services, Google, and Microsoft in the cloud-native database market. It analyzes customer spending data from Enterprise Technology Research (ETR) to demonstrate Snowflake's strong spending momentum across all three major clouds and discusses its strategy of being cloud-agnostic and prioritizing engineering investments. The piece concludes that Snowflake's specialized focus and native cloud architecture position it well for continued growth and a successful IPO despite competition from giants with vast R&D budgets.

title: Mobile Gaming: Innovation in Action
summary: Mobile gaming has become the largest and fastest-growing gaming platform due to continuous innovation and its accessibility, especially in emerging markets. Companies like Tencent, NetEase, and Sea Limited are capitalizing on this boom. The article suggests that Mobile gaming is demonstrating resilience and continued growth in various market conditions, making a diversified investment approach attractive.

title: Amazon sues to limit former AWS marketing VP Brian Hall’s new job at Google Cloud
summary: Amazon.com Inc. has filed a lawsuit against Brian Hall, a former VP of product marketing at Amazon Web Services Inc., to prevent him from taking a new role at Google Cloud due to a noncompete agreement. The lawsuit claims Hall's move risks exposing "valuable competitive information" related to Amazon's cloud product roadmap and strategy. Hall's lawyers argue the noncompete clause is overbroad and unenforceable, citing prior assurances from an AWS executive and Amazon's non-enforcement against another executive who joined a rival.

title: Rackspace rebrands (again) and repositions for digital transformation
summary: Rackspace has rebranded itself as Rackspace Technology and repositioned its strategy to focus on end-to-end technology solutions across four key areas, including cloud optimization, security, cloud-native enablement, and data modernization. This move follows a series of acquisitions and strategic partnerships, as the company prepares for a potential new initial public offering. The company aims to tackle the entire technology transformation lifecycle for its customers.

title: NTT DATA and Microsoft announce strategic collaboration to enable new digital solutions
summary: NTT DATA and Microsoft have announced an expanded strategic collaboration to accelerate enterprise digital transformation. The alliance will leverage Microsoft Azure, Microsoft 365, Microsoft Teams, and Dynamics 365 with NTT DATA's IT services to enhance business operations, productivity, and workstyle innovation. Key initiatives include client digital transformation, workstyle innovation within NTT DATA, capability development for 10,000 NTT DATA employees, and "Technology For Good" initiatives focusing on AI for Health.

title: Mitsubishi Electric to acquire plant from Sharp to boost EV power chip output
summary: Mitsubishi Electric Corp announced it would acquire two idled facilities from Sharp's chip plant for approximately 20 billion yen ($187 million) to boost its production of power management chips for electric vehicles (EVs). This strategic move aims to meet the increasing demand for these critical components, with the new plant expected to commence operations in November of the following year. The expansion positions Mitsubishi to compete with rivals like Infineon Technologies AG and ON Semiconductor Corp, which are also expanding their power chip manufacturing capabilities.

title: Tencent buys $200m+ stake in Warner Music Group (update)
summary: Tencent, through its Music Entertainment subsidiary and Huang River Investment Limited, has acquired 8 million Class A common stock shares in Warner Music Group, totaling a stake of 10.4% of Class A shares and 1.6% of WMG overall, in a transaction valued at over $200 million. This acquisition deepens the complex web of cross-ownership within the music industry, with Tencent, Warner, Sony, Universal, Spotify, and Epic Games holding various stakes in each other.

title: How Qualcomm (QCOM) Is Helping Small Businesses Convert To Mobile-First Work Environments
summary: Qualcomm (QCOM) has launched the Qualcomm Small Business Accelerator Program to help small businesses transition to mobile-first work environments. This program will provide selected businesses with products powered by Qualcomm Technologies solutions, along with collaboration tools and technical support valued at up to $25,000. Key partners like Citrix, Lenovo, Linksys, Samsung, Sophos, and Targus, along with Best Buy Business, Microsoft, and Verizon Business, are supporting this initiative to bolster economic growth and productivity for small businesses, especially during the current global pandemic.

title: The Netflix of China skyrockets 38% after Tencent eyes potential investment, report says
summary: Shares of iQIYI, often called the "Netflix of China," surged 38% after a Reuters report indicated that Tencent is considering a significant investment in the company. Tencent aims to become the largest investor in iQIYI to reduce competition and lower costs in the booming video streaming market amid the coronavirus pandemic. Talks are reportedly in early stages between Tencent and Baidu, iQIYI's current majority shareholder.

title: Announcing the Citizen Care Pod, a New COVID-19 Smart Screening and Testing Pod Combining Intelligent Technology with Modular Design – Microsoft News Center Canada
summary: A collaboration between Citizen Care Pod Corporation, WZMH Architects, PCL Construction, Insight Enterprises, and Microsoft has led to the launch of the Citizen Care Pod. This smart screening and testing pod integrates intelligent technology within a modular design to support COVID-19 testing, screening, and eventual vaccination on a mass scale, aiming for a safe economic recovery. The customizable units, retrofitted from shipping containers, utilize Microsoft Azure cloud platform and AI for safety and efficiency, with potential applications beyond the current pandemic.

title: Oracle expects flat sales on fewer corporate software deals
summary: Oracle Corp. projects flat revenue in the current quarter due to delayed software purchases by corporate clients amid the coronavirus pandemic. The company, the world's second-biggest software-maker, reported a 6.3% decline in fiscal fourth-quarter revenue, missing analyst estimates. Oracle is struggling to shift existing database customers to cloud-based offerings and compete with Amazon.com Inc. and Microsoft Corp.

title: Samsung Announces Range of Back-to-Business Commercial Display Solutions
summary: Samsung Electronics America, Inc. announced a variety of commercial display solutions designed to help businesses reopen by focusing on safety, collaboration, and communication. These solutions include temperature screening kiosks, collaborative tools like Webex on Flip, and versatile Pro TV displays for streaming content and promoting safety guidelines. The offerings aim to equip businesses with tools for successful and efficient operations in the current climate.

title: This NAACP-backed ETF will help you invest in companies that care about equality
summary: The Impact Shares NAACP Minority Empowerment ETF (NACP) allows investors to support companies committed to diversity and racial equality. Developed in partnership with the NAACP and Impact Shares, the ETF screens companies based on their practices in hiring, pay, promotion, and supply chains, with net proceeds going to the NAACP for social advocacy. With over $4 million in net assets and holdings in major companies like Amazon and Microsoft, the fund aims to achieve "social alpha" by investing in corporate leaders in social justice.

title: Xtrackers MSCI Kokusai Equity ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:KOKU)
summary: The Xtrackers MSCI Kokusai Equity ETF (KOKU) tracks a market cap-weighted index of large and mid-cap developed market stocks globally, excluding Japan. Launched on April 8, 2020, KOKU has $823.01 million in market capitalization and a net expense ratio of 0.09%. Its top holdings include major tech companies like Apple, NVIDIA, and Microsoft.

title: Trump signs order freezing visas for foreign workers through the end of the year
summary: President Donald Trump signed an executive order freezing new visas for various foreign workers, including tech and low-skill jobs, through the end of 2020. This action, aiming to preserve jobs amidst the COVID-19 economic downturn, exempts specific essential workers but includes au pairs and certain other exchange programs. The policy is expected to face backlash from the business community and immigration advocates despite the White House's claim of saving or creating 525,000 American jobs.

title: Adobe Flash Player ends officially on December 31, 2020
summary: Adobe announced that support for its Flash Player will officially end on December 31, 2020. Users are advised to uninstall the software by then, as Flash Player downloads will be removed from Adobe's website, and Flash-based content will be blocked from running after the end-of-life date. Major browser vendors like Google and Mozilla are also removing Flash support from their products.

title: Awash in “AI Platforms”
summary: This article discusses the booming market for "AI Platforms," noting the significant financial investments predicted for digital transformation software by 2025. It criticizes the proliferation of open-source "AI Platforms" which, while offering useful components, individually lack the comprehensive utility required to fully develop and operate enterprise AI and IoT applications. The author argues that many of these components were not designed to work together and highlights their commercial viability issues.

title: Malaysia builds its Mass Transit System in the Microsoft Cloud
summary: Malaysia's Mass Rapid Transit Corporation (MRTC) is using Microsoft Azure and Bentley Systems' software to design and build the newest extension of its Greater Kuala Lumpur regional rail line. This cloud-based approach has enabled 1,500 engineers to collaborate using a connected data environment, reducing errors, improving collaboration efficiency by 35 percent, and ensuring the project stays on time and within budget. The system helps manage 7,500 models and over 280,000 documents, leading to a significant reduction in service clashes.

title: Malaysia builds its Mass Transit System in the Microsoft Cloud
summary: Malaysia's Mass Rapid Transit Corporation (MRTC) is using Microsoft Azure and Bentley Systems' solutions to design and build an extension to its Greater Kuala Lumpur regional rail line. This cloud-based approach allows for improved collaboration among 1,500 engineers and construction managers, reducing errors and design conflicts, boosting efficiency by 35 percent, and ensuring the project stays on schedule and within budget. The system helps manage 2.3 terabytes of project data and aims to enhance asset performance and reliability for the new SSP Line.

title: Vornado explores sale of office buildings co-owned with Trump Org.
summary: Vornado Realty Trust is considering selling its office buildings in New York and San Francisco, which are co-owned with the Trump Organization. Vornado holds a 70% controlling interest in these properties, with the Trump Organization possessing a 30% passive stake. This potential sale comes as Vornado's shares have dropped and concerns about the real estate market's recovery from the pandemic persist.

title: Apple, Google and chorus of tech business leaders slam Trump's new visa restrictions
summary: Tech giants Apple and Google, along with other prominent business leaders, criticized the Trump administration's new restrictions on work visas, including the H-1B and L-1 visas. Critics argue that these restrictions, implemented to free up jobs for American workers, will actually hinder job creation and economic growth. CEOs like Tim Cook, Sundar Pichai, Brad Smith, Marc Benioff, and Elon Musk all expressed disappointment, highlighting the positive contributions of immigrant workers to innovation and the U.S. economy.

title: HPE Builds Out GreenLake Utility, Creates Ezmeral Software
summary: HPE is accelerating its transformation into a platform provider, offering its entire portfolio as a service by 2022 through its GreenLake cloud-like platform. The company is significantly expanding GreenLake's services with new offerings and launched a new software portfolio under the brand name HPE Ezmeral, aimed at modern workloads like container orchestration, AI, and MLOps. This move strengthens HPE's competition in the enterprise Kubernetes space and leverages acquisitions like BlueData and MapR to create an integrated, open-source oriented solution for cloud-native and non-cloud applications.

title: Lessons Learned from Zscaler's Recent Success
summary: Zscaler's recent success is attributed to solid financials, strategic acquisitions, and increasing demand for its cloud-based endpoint security, especially with the rise of remote work. The company's impressive partnership roster also plays a key role, though it faces competition from both integrated partners and hardware-based cybersecurity incumbents.

title: Honeywell claims it has built the most powerful quantum computer ever
summary: Honeywell claims to have built the most powerful quantum computer to date, boasting a quantum volume of 64, double that of the next highest IBM quantum computer. While this achievement is significant for Honeywell's internal operations, researchers remain skeptical as the computer's six qubits cannot yet perform calculations beyond the capability of classical computers, unlike Google's 53-qubit machine that achieved quantum supremacy. Despite this, Honeywell views it as an important step towards integrating quantum computing into their industries.

title: FORD UNLOCKS POTENTIAL OF 5G TO FUTURE-PROOF ELECTRIC VEHICLE PRODUCTION
summary: Ford, in partnership with Vodafone Business, has secured government backing to implement 5G connectivity in its electric vehicle manufacturing processes. This initiative, part of the new E:PriME facility on Ford’s Dunton Campus, aims to enhance speed, accuracy, and control in EV production, particularly for welding processes, which generate vast amounts of data. The move is expected to transform manufacturing flexibility and facilitate the deployment of next-generation systems with remote expert support and AI.

title: J2 Global: Troubling Related Party Transactions, Looming Impairments And A Suspicious History Of Insider Enrichment Spanning Decades
summary: Hindenburg Research exposes J2 Global's alleged history of insider self-enrichment, related-party transactions, and questionable accounting practices. The report details how J2's opaque acquisition system, led by its VP of Corporate Development, may have facilitated millions in insider gains, while key business metrics decline and significant impairments remain undisclosed at the parent company level despite being recorded by subsidiaries. The article also highlights severe corporate governance issues, including conflicted independent board members and the CEO's exorbitant compensation.

title: How Cloud Computing changes the way of business at Porsche
summary: Porsche is increasingly adopting cloud computing, viewing it as a critical enabler for innovation and digital transformation. The company hosted its first Cloud Innovation Day to educate employees, demonstrate its impact on the automotive industry, and explore its potential for enhancing customer experiences and internal operations. Porsche emphasizes that cloudification involves not just technology but also organizational and cultural adjustments.

title: F5 patches vulnerability that received a CVSS 10 severity score
summary: F5 Networks has issued a critical security advisory for its BIG-IP product, urging customers to patch a vulnerability (CVE-2020-5902) that received a CVSSv3 score of 10. This remote code execution flaw in the TMUI management interface could allow attackers to gain full control over affected devices without authentication, impacting government, cloud providers, ISPs, banks, and Fortune 500 companies. The urgency for patching is extremely high due to the ease of exploitation and the potential for severe system compromise and data interception.

title: Attackers are breaching F5 BIG-IP devices, check whether you’ve been hit
summary: Attackers are actively exploiting CVE-2020-5902, a critical remote code execution vulnerability in F5 Networks' BIG-IP devices, to install coin-miners, IoT malware, or scrape credentials. This vulnerability affects the Traffic Management User Interface (TMUI) of BIG-IP devices, allowing unauthorized remote code execution. Companies are urged to patch immediately and perform checks for compromise, as attackers are also bypassing some previously suggested mitigations.

title: Google, Deutsche Bank Agree to 10-Year Cloud Partnership
summary: Google and Deutsche Bank have entered a 10-year cloud partnership, with Google providing cloud computing capabilities to Germany's largest lender. Deutsche Bank anticipates a cumulative return on investment of €1 billion ($1.1 billion) from this alliance, considering it both a revenue growth and cost-saving initiative. This deal represents a significant win for Google in the financial sector, as European banks increasingly adopt cloud solutions to modernize their IT infrastructure.

title: Chicago Quantum Exchange announces seven new partnerships to advance research, training
summary: The Chicago Quantum Exchange (CQE), a research hub based at the University of Chicago, has announced seven new corporate partnerships to advance quantum technology research and development. These new partners include Intel, JPMorgan Chase, Microsoft, Quantum Design, Qubitekk, Rigetti Computing, and Zurich Instruments, expanding CQE's collaborations to a total of 13 companies. The partnerships aim to accelerate discovery, develop quantum applications, and prepare a skilled quantum workforce by leveraging expertise from universities, national laboratories, and industry leaders.

title: Smart investment during a pandemic
summary: Franklin Templeton advocates for a well-diversified global investment portfolio to navigate market uncertainties during a pandemic. They suggest adopting "Defend, Diversify, and Buffer" strategies to protect investments and seize opportunities in sectors like technology and emerging markets. The article emphasizes long-term trends and the benefits of professional fund management over market timing.

title: The 10 Biggest Networking Company Acquisitions Of 2020 (So Far)
summary: This article details the 10 biggest networking company acquisitions of 2020 to date, highlighting significant deals made by tech giants like Nvidia, Cisco, and F5 Networks. It covers purchases ranging from billion-dollar agreements to more strategic acquisitions aimed at expanding portfolios in areas like 5G, cloud security, and software-defined networking, despite the economic downturn caused by the global pandemic. The acquisitions underscore the dynamic nature of the networking market and companies' efforts to enhance their services and product offerings.

title: monday.com integrates to Microsoft Teams -
summary: monday.com has announced the integration of Microsoft Teams into its Work OS platform. This collaboration allows users to access monday.com features directly within Teams and receive notifications, aiming to streamline workflows and improve collaboration. The integration is seen as a significant step for monday.com towards closer ties with Microsoft, with other existing integrations including Microsoft Azure AD, Microsoft Outlook, and OneDrive.

title: Irving-based firm shutters without warning while working on a major COVID-19 study
summary: Irving-based health data company, Examination Management Services Inc. (EMSI), abruptly closed on July 3rd, citing economic fallout from the coronavirus pandemic. This closure has caused significant delays in a crucial COVID-19 study led by Microsoft and Adaptive Biotechnologies Corp., which was relying on EMSI to collect 1,000 blood samples to understand the immune response to the virus. Former employees have filed a class-action lawsuit against EMSI for unpaid wages and lack of proper notice for mass layoffs.

title: NVIDIA Now Most Valuable US Chipmaker, Intel Falls Behind
summary: NVIDIA has overtaken Intel to become the most valuable U.S. chipmaker, with its market capitalization reaching $251.3 billion compared to Intel's $248.2 billion. This surge is attributed to NVIDIA's strong financial performance, its dominance in gaming and data center markets, rapid adoption of its GPUs in AI, efficient cost management, and robust cash flow. The company's stock has shown exceptional growth, rallying 73.7% year-to-date and over twenty-fold in the last five years.

title: Eli Lilly CEO on raising $1 billion for antibiotic research: Goal is to have two to four new antibiotics by 2030
summary: Eli Lilly CEO David Ricks discussed the company's efforts to raise $1 billion for antibiotic research. The goal is to develop two to four new antibiotics by 2030. This initiative comes as biopharma firms are intensifying antibiotic research funding, especially amidst the coronavirus pandemic.

title: Tech Moves: Zillow co-founder joins Palantir board; Hootsuite names new CEO; and more
summary: This article details significant personnel changes and appointments within the Pacific Northwest tech community and beyond. Key moves include Zillow co-founder Spencer Rascoff joining Palantir Technologies' board, Hootsuite appointing Tom Keiser as its new CEO, and various other executive changes at companies like Intellectual Ventures, Qumulo, Avalara, and Capitolis. The report covers a range of positions from COOs and CMOs to directors and product managers, highlighting a dynamic period of leadership adjustments in the technology sector.

title: Marc Benioff's Salesforce has eclipsed Larry Ellison's Oracle in market cap
summary: Salesforce's market capitalization has surpassed Oracle's, marking a significant milestone in the long-standing rivalry between Marc Benioff and Larry Ellison. Salesforce, under Benioff, has grown by diversifying its offerings and validating its internet-delivered software model, achieving profitability and expanding its market share even as some analysts suggest avenues for greater profit margins. This development highlights Salesforce's success despite its younger age compared to Oracle, a company that Ellison acknowledged missing the initial cloud trend.

title: Apple CEO Tim Cook No.2 on 2019 highest paid list at $133.7 million
summary: Apple CEO Tim Cook ranked second on the 2019 highest-paid executive list with $133.7 million, largely due to an equity grant he received in 2011. Elon Musk topped the list with $595.3 million, primarily from a pay deal tied to Tesla's valuation. The article highlights the significant compensation packages in the tech industry compared to other sectors like finance.

title: Rackspace Technology Files For IPO Four Years After Going Private
summary: Rackspace Technology, a managed cloud company, has filed for an initial public offering four years after going private.
