title: Suite Hub streamlines bookings and increases conversions with Dynamics 365 Sales and Power Apps
summary: Suite Hub, a serviced accommodation booking platform, has leveraged Microsoft Dynamics 365 Sales and Power Apps to enhance its operations. By unifying its interface and implementing Power Automate flows, Suite Hub achieved a 30% increase in booking conversions and over 60% greater efficiency in its booking processes. This integration has also improved data security and agility, allowing the company to better serve both corporate bookers and accommodation providers.

title: Microsoft Promises Greater PC Security with Coming Pluton Processors
summary: Microsoft is introducing Pluton, a security solution designed to enhance PC security by integrating the root of trust directly into the CPU, making devices more resistant to physical tampering. Historically used in Xbox and Azure Sphere, Pluton aims to address vulnerabilities found in traditional Trusted Platform Modules (TPMs) by eliminating the external bus communication that can be exploited. Microsoft is collaborating with AMD, Intel, and Qualcomm to bring this chip-to-cloud security technology to future Windows PCs and Azure datacenters.

title: Microsoft developing ‘Pluton’ security chip for Windows
summary: Microsoft is developing a new specialized security chip called "Pluton" for Windows computers, intended to be built directly into the main processor. Pluton aims to replace the current TPM security coprocessors and enhance protection against exploits like Meltdown and Spectre by eliminating the bus interface vulnerability. Microsoft is collaborating with Intel, AMD, and Qualcomm to integrate Pluton, with firmware updates delivered via Windows updates.

title: Congratulations to Our 2020 Global Partners of the Year!
summary: Palo Alto Networks recognized its 2020 Global Partners of the Year at the Ignite '20 Partner Summit for their excellence in delivering and integrating solutions. The awards highlighted partners who safeguard networks, offer cloud-native security, and enable autonomous SOCs, with a record number of attendees at the virtual event. For the first time, a Global Social Impact Award was also presented to acknowledge efforts that made a positive difference in 2020.

title: DataStax optimizes Cassandra for Kubernetes with K8ssandra
summary: DataStax has launched K8ssandra, a new project designed to simplify the deployment and management of the open-source Cassandra database on Kubernetes platforms. K8ssandra combines monitoring tools, helm charts, and an operator, integrating components like Cassandra Reaper, Medusa backup tool, and Grafana for enhanced visibility. This initiative aims to address the complexities users face when running Cassandra in Kubernetes environments by packaging essential tools and expertise.

title: Looking Closer At T. Rowe Price's Dividend Growth ETF, 'TDVG'
summary: The T. Rowe Price Dividend Growth ETF (TDVG), launched in August 2020, is an actively managed ETF that seeks dividend income and long-term capital growth by investing in dividend-paying companies expected to increase their dividends over time. Managed by Tom Huber, this ETF typically holds 100-125 stocks like Microsoft, Apple, and Visa, focusing on business model durability and financial health with a "growth-at-a-discount" approach. It's designed for investors seeking a mix of income and capital appreciation from an experienced management team.

title: Apple to lower App Store fees for small developers, but some critics not impressed
summary: Apple announced a new program to lower its App Store commission to 15% for software developers who make $1 million US or less in proceeds annually. While some hail this as a "huge win" for smaller developers, critics like Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney and Spotify Technology SA dismissed it as "window dressing" and a calculated move to preserve Apple's monopoly and divide app creators. The change affects a large percentage of developers but a small portion of Apple's overall App Store revenue.

title: Nuance to sell transcription, EHR go-live services businesses
summary: Nuance Communications announced its intention to sell its transcription and EHR go-live services businesses. This strategic move allows Nuance to focus on its core healthcare artificial intelligence solutions. The divestiture aims to streamline its operations and enhance its position in the evolving health tech market.

title: Compass elects LinkedIn CFO Steve Sordello to board of directors
summary: Real estate technology firm Compass has appointed Steve Sordello, LinkedIn's CFO, to its board of directors. Sordello brings extensive experience from his tenure at LinkedIn, where he oversaw the company's IPO and its $26.2 billion merger with Microsoft. His expertise in guiding fast-growing businesses will be instrumental as Compass continues to expand and empower its real estate agents.

title: Phillips 66 Enables Google Pay at the Pump
summary: Phillips 66 has partnered with P97 Networks to integrate Google Pay at its 7,000 Phillips 66, Conoco, and 76 branded gas stations. This new capability allows drivers to use the Google Pay app on both Android and iOS to locate stations, fuel up, and pay, significantly enhancing the fueling experience. Donald Frieden, CEO of P97, highlighted the innovation as a foundation for future mobility solutions.

title: Compass elects LinkedIn CFO Steve Sordello to board of directors
summary: Real estate technology firm Compass has appointed LinkedIn CFO Steve Sordello to its board of directors. Sordello brings extensive experience from LinkedIn, where he oversaw its IPO and merger with Microsoft, as well as previous CFO roles at TiVo, Inc. and Ask Jeeves, Inc. This appointment marks Sordello as the fourth independent board member to join Compass in 2020, aiming to leverage his expertise in guiding fast-growing businesses that serve large groups of professionals.

title: Now that's multicloud: CIA awards multibillion-dollar contract to AWS, Microsoft, Google, Oracle and IBM
summary: The CIA has awarded its Commercial Cloud Enterprise (C2E) contract to Amazon Web Services, Microsoft, Google, Oracle, and IBM, marking a significant shift to a multicloud strategy. This multibillion-dollar contract allows these five major public cloud providers to compete for task orders from the CIA and 16 other intelligence agencies across different security classification levels. This move aims to leverage the unique strengths of various providers for different workloads and enhance competition, contrasting with past single-vendor awards like the Department of Defense's JEDI contract.

title: Why Rackspace Revenue Growth Has Slowed Down
summary: Rackspace's revenue growth has slowed despite the increasing preference for cloud services due to a change in its strategy, which includes offering bundled computing and support services and potentially higher pricing compared to competitors. The company had considered a merger or buyout in 2014 but ultimately decided against it, opting to appoint a new CEO, Taylor Rhodes, to lead its revised operational strategy.

title: Graphical Representation of General Electric’s Business Model
summary: This article outlines General Electric's business model, highlighting its two main divisions: industrials and finance services, which contributed 91% and 9% respectively to its consolidated 2015 earnings. It details GE's industrial backlog, geographic reach, core strengths, and competitiveness, along with its 2016 operating EPS target. The company's strategic focus on technology, growth markets, and services is emphasized.

title: General Electric’s Mission, Vision, and Strategy
summary: General Electric (GE) is undergoing a strategic transformation to shift from a broad conglomerate to a focused industrial leader. This involves reshaping its portfolio by acquiring businesses like Alstom’s Power and Grid, spinning off entities like Synchrony Financial, and divesting non-strategic segments such as its appliance business. The goal is to achieve 75% of operating EPS from industrial businesses and return $50 billion to investors.

title: The Value of Data in a Digital World
summary: This article discusses the increasing value of data in a digital world, contrasting it with the historical valuation of companies based on tangible assets. It explores why data should be considered an asset, despite current accounting rules, and proposes three approaches for data valuation: market-based, cost-based, and cash flow-based, providing examples for each. The article also touches on how data-rich enterprises can seize opportunities and mentions related ETFs that invest in data-centric technologies.

title: Gov. Hogan names College Park quantum computing company one of top state start-ups
summary: Maryland Gov. Larry Hogan recognized IonQ, a College Park quantum computing company, as one of the top 20 start-up companies in the state. IonQ, based in the Discovery District, is developing quantum computers and software, including a system currently working with both Amazon and Microsoft. The university has invested $5.5 million in the company and utilizes its research, contributing to College Park's aim to become a quantum computing hub.

title: Forget FAANG—it’s time to scale MT SAAS
summary: Bessemer Venture Partners introduces "MT SAAS" (Microsoft, Twilio, Salesforce, Amazon, Adobe, Shopify) as the new basket of top public technology companies, succeeding the traditional "FAANG" stocks. This new group represents leaders in cloud computing, identified as the mega-trend of the next decade, and has shown significant outperformance compared to FAANG stocks over recent years. The article details the characteristics and growth trajectories of each MT SAAS company, highlighting their cloud-first strategies and substantial market capitalization gains.

title: Microsoft 365 specialist AvePoint to go public through $2B SPAC merger
summary: AvePoint Inc., a software provider for managing Microsoft 365 deployments, announced its plan to go public through a $2 billion SPAC merger with Apex Technology Acquisition Corp. This deal will provide AvePoint with $352 million from Apex and an additional $140 million from institutional investors, resulting in $252 million cash on its balance sheet. The company, which specializes in securing business data, managing Microsoft Teams, and migrating legacy data, expects to close the year with $148 million in revenue, a 26% increase from 2019, and plans to use the capital for engineering and international expansion.

title: Microsoft Teams Leader in Gartner UCaaS and Meetings Magic Quadrants
summary: Microsoft Teams has been recognized as a leader in both the Gartner Unified Communications as a Service (UCaaS) and Meeting Solutions Magic Quadrants. This marks Microsoft's second consecutive year as a UCaaS leader and its fourteenth time recognized as a leader for Meetings Solutions. The article details Microsoft Teams' strengths and cautions noted by Gartner in both categories.

title: Microsoft 365 Cloud Partner AvePoint Merges at $2B Valuation
summary: AvePoint, a cloud solutions provider supporting over 7 million Microsoft 365 users, has merged with Apex Technology Acquisition Corporation in a deal valuing AvePoint at $2 billion. The merger is expected to close in Q1 2021, with AvePoint retaining its name and trading on Nasdaq under the ticker "AVPT." This move highlights the growing demand for Microsoft cloud solutions and AvePoint's strong financial performance and strategic market position.

title: Smart City Platform Market May See a Big Move | Cisco Systems, Intel, NEC
summary: The Global Smart City Platform Market was valued at approximately USD 124.7 billion in 2019 and is projected to grow at over 11.2% annually from 2020 to 2027. Key drivers include rising urban populations, the increasing adoption of IoT technology, and digital transformations. Major players like Cisco Systems, IBM, Siemens, Hitachi, Microsoft, Schneider Electric, Huawei, Intel, NEC, and Amazon Web Services are profiled in a new HTF MI report.

title: Lindsay Corp. unveils Smart Pivot
summary: Lindsay Corp. has introduced its Smart Pivot system, an autonomous crop management system developed in partnership with Microsoft Azure and Taranis. This system uses satellite imagery, aerial imagery, and pivot-mounted sensors to monitor crop health, detect anomalies, streamline irrigation decisions, and reduce operational downtime in agricultural fields. The Smart Pivot aims to transform traditional center pivots into intelligent, networked robots that can identify and address issues before they become significant problems, ultimately saving resources and improving efficiency for growers.

title: Should you invest in technology sector funds?
summary: This article discusses the performance and prospects of technology sector funds in India, highlighting their strong returns during the pandemic and the factors influencing their growth. It explores investment options including domestic and international tech funds, the outlook for Indian IT firms, and crucial risks and investment strategies investors should consider, such as staggering investments via SIPs.

title: BHP highlights importance of resilient & innovative supply chain partnerships in the COVID-19 era
summary: BHP's Group Procurement Officer, Sundeep Singh, emphasized the critical role of resilient and innovative supply chain partnerships during the COVID-19 pandemic. He noted that while cost-effectiveness and reliability are important, truly resilient supply chains require a culture of partnership to navigate disruptions, ensure safety, and unlock shared value through collaboration and innovation. Singh highlighted examples such as the partnership with Compass for facility management and the 'Supplier Illumination program' that leveraged AI and Deloitte to increase supply chain transparency and resilience.

title: Ozon IPO Is First U.S. Listing Of A Russian-Based Firm In 18 Months
summary: Russian e-commerce company Ozon Holdings (OZON) successfully raised $990 million in its initial public offering, marking the first U.S. listing by a Russian-based firm in 18 months. The IPO began trading on Tuesday afternoon. Ozon's listing on U.S. domestic exchanges breaks a dry spell for Russian IPOs since May 2019.

title: Dow pulls back more than 150 points after reaching 30,000 milestone
summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell on Wednesday, pulling back after reaching the 30,000 milestone the previous day, amidst disappointing unemployment data. The S&P 500 dipped while the Nasdaq Composite rose, and trading volumes were lighter ahead of Thanksgiving. Salesforce led the Dow lower on news of its potential acquisition of Slack, while positive vaccine news and political clarity had previously fueled market rallies.

title: EA SPORTS FIFA 21 Delivers the Most Authentic Matchday Experience to Date Through the Power of Next Generation Hardware
summary: Electronic Arts announced that EA Sports FIFA 21 will launch on PlayStation®5 and Xbox® Series X|S on December 4, leveraging next-gen console power and the Frostbite engine for an authentic matchday experience. The game will feature lightning-fast load times, enhanced visuals and audio, and realistic player movement, immersing fans in The World's Game like never before. Players who own FIFA 21 on PS4 or Xbox One can get the next-gen version for free, retaining their FUT Club and VOLTA FOOTBALL progress.

title: A|I: The AI Times – The AI that fails to see women at all
summary: This article compiles the latest news in AI, machine learning, big data, and automation. Key topics include DarwinAI's partnership with Red Hat to deploy a COVID-19 solution, research from the University of Alberta on using machine learning to fill in public health data, and Rockwell Automation's acquisition of Toronto-based Fiix Inc. A central concern highlighted is the bias in AI image recognition that misinterprets women, along with Roche's new AI and digital health initiative, Autodesk's acquisition of Spacemaker, and the LAPD's ban on commercial facial recognition.

title: Findings: 2020 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Access Management
summary: The article reviews the 2020 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Access Management, highlighting changes since the 2019 report and Gartner's definition of Access Management. It details vendor placements across the Niche Players, Challengers, and Leaders quadrants, noting significant shifts and key strengths for companies like OneLogin, ForgeRock, Okta, Ping Identity, Microsoft, Oracle, CyberArk, IBM, Auth0, Thales, and Micro Focus. The report also discusses market trends such as the increasing adoption of AM as a Service and the projected rise of UEBA capabilities in workforce access management.

title: NHN, Intel team up to take on cloud business
summary: South Korean IT company NHN Corp. and Intel Corp. have formed a strategic partnership to expand their presence in the cloud market. This collaboration includes product development like NHN's new DaaS powered by Intel Optane, the launch of the AI-driven Toast Cloud Center 2, and a focus on global market expansion. The move comes as cloud computing services are experiencing significant growth, with many tech giants investing in data centers in Korea.

title: Microsoft announced as a member of GAIA-X
summary: Microsoft has been announced as a member of GAIA-X, a project focused on creating a federated data and cloud infrastructure to benefit Europe. Microsoft supports GAIA-X's vision for European economic growth and digital transformation. Casper Klynge, Vice President European Government Affairs, stated Microsoft's commitment to building "Tech Fit 4 Europe."

title: Top-Selling Videogames of the Last 25 Years Show Mario and Call of Duty Rule
summary: A report on the top-selling videogames over the past 25 years reveals the dominance of franchises like Super Mario and Call of Duty. While new games are constantly released, sequels and reboots from major publishers such as Activision Blizzard, Electronic Arts, and Nintendo consistently lead sales charts. The article also highlights the significant growth of mobile gaming revenue and the burgeoning popularity of live-streaming and esports viewership.

title: With Slack, Salesforce Would Put Heat on Microsoft
summary: Salesforce.com Inc.'s potential acquisition of Slack Technologies Inc., valued at $17 billion, positions Salesforce to directly challenge Microsoft Corp. in the business-software market. This strategic move by CEO Marc Benioff, leveraging the work-from-home trend, aims to make Salesforce a dominant provider and intensify competition with its long-time rival. The Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday that Salesforce is in advanced talks to buy Slack.

title: Alphabet’s (Google’s) first catastrophe bond priced on-target at $237.5m
summary: Alphabet (Google's parent company) has successfully priced its first catastrophe bond, Phoenician Re Ltd. (Series 2020-1), at the target size of $237.5 million. This cat bond will provide Alphabet with California earthquake insurance protection through its captive insurer and Hannover Re, marking a significant step for a major tech company entering the catastrophe bond market for efficient risk transfer. The bond offers a 3% coupon to investors across a three-year term.

title: Rockwell touts its role helping suppliers to AstraZeneca, others scale up for Covid-19 vaccines
summary: Rockwell Automation, a Milwaukee-based industrial automation firm, is experiencing increased sales of its products and services to pharmaceutical company suppliers, including AstraZeneca PLC. This growth is attributed to the demand for scaling up Covid-19 vaccine development and manufacturing efforts. While not directly involved in vaccine creation, Rockwell plays a crucial role in enabling its partners to meet production needs.

title: Is Zoom a Chinese Company?
summary: This article addresses the common question of whether Zoom Video Communications Inc. is a Chinese company, clarifying its U.S. base despite its founder's origins and global operations. It also delves into Zoom's history, its market competitors, and its freemium business model, particularly highlighting how the COVID-19 pandemic fueled its growth. The piece concludes by touching on Zoom's tax collection practices in the U.S.

title: Zoom has picked Amazon Web Services as its preferred cloud provider, months after forming a partnership with Oracle
summary: Zoom has chosen Amazon Web Services (AWS) as its preferred cloud provider, despite having formed a significant partnership with Oracle months earlier to handle increased traffic during the pandemic. This new multi-year agreement strengthens Zoom's long-standing relationship with AWS, integrating new AI features into its Zoom Rooms product via Alexa for Business. While Zoom continues to use other cloud services like Oracle and Microsoft Azure, designating AWS as preferred signals a deeper commitment, driven by AWS's scalability in handling Zoom's massive growth during the pandemic.

title: ServiceNow is acquiring Element AI, the Canadian startup building AI services for enterprises
summary: ServiceNow is acquiring Element AI, a Canadian startup specializing in AI services for enterprises, to strengthen its automation and AI capabilities. The deal, estimated at $500 million, will integrate Element AI's technical talent into ServiceNow and establish an AI Innovation Hub in Montreal. This acquisition is part of ServiceNow's broader strategy to position itself as a leader in digital transformation and enterprise IT services.

title: How Cloud Is Democratizing RDMA Use in the Financial Services Industry
summary: The financial services industry is seeing Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) become more accessible due to cloud migration, enabling smaller firms to leverage a technology previously exclusive to large institutions. NASDAQ's move to the cloud by 2030 highlights this trend. RDMA's high performance and low latency capabilities can be applied beyond high-frequency trading to areas like risk modeling, portfolio rebalancing, and payments, democratizing advanced computing power.

title: Salesforce buying Slack in $27.7B deal in work from home bet
summary: Salesforce announced its acquisition of Slack for $27.7 billion, a move largely driven by the increasing shift to remote work and the "work-from-anywhere world." Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff stated the deal would "shape the future of enterprise software," while Slack CEO Stewart Butterfield highlighted the massive opportunity presented by the combined entities. This acquisition is poised to intensify competition with Microsoft's Teams product and signifies a long-term bet on remote work trends.

title: LivePerson's 2020 Consumer Preferences for Conversational Commerce report reveals skyrocketing demand for messaging and conversational AI
summary: LivePerson's 2020 Consumer Preferences for Conversational Commerce report indicates a significant increase in demand for messaging and conversational AI, with 85% of consumers worldwide wanting to message with brands, up from 65% in 2019. The report highlights that a large majority of consumers would spend more with brands offering messaging options and also notes expanding use cases for conversational AI beyond customer service to marketing and sales. Consumers value the speed and convenience of bots but desire more human empathy and personality in their interactions.

title: Why Dimensional Fund Advisors is converting six of its mutual funds to the ETF format
summary: Dimensional Fund Advisors is converting six mutual funds to ETFs as part of an industry-first move, building on the success of its newly launched transparent, actively managed ETFs like DFAU and DFAI. The conversion aims to offer investors the benefits of indexing combined with active management, as requested by financial professionals, and capitalizes on the strong performance of value stocks.

title: Salesforce buys Slack in a $27.7B megadeal
summary: Salesforce has announced its acquisition of Slack for $27.7 billion, a deal that leadership from both companies described as historical and visionary for the future of enterprise software. This acquisition comes after Slack's struggles with public valuation and competition, positioning Salesforce more directly against rivals like Microsoft Teams. The deal aims to enhance Salesforce's social offerings and integrate communication more deeply into its customer relationship management ecosystem.

title: Vancouverite Stewart Butterfield’s Slack sold to Salesforce for US$27.7b
summary: Salesforce.com Inc. is acquiring messaging service Slack Technologies Inc. in a cash-and-stock deal valued at US$27.7 billion. Slack's CEO and Vancouverite Stewart Butterfield will continue to lead the unit after the acquisition, which is expected to close during the second quarter of 2022. The deal aims to strengthen Slack's position against competitors like Microsoft in the business-messaging sector.

title: Salesforce acquires Slack for over $27 billion, marking cloud software vendor's largest deal ever
summary: Salesforce announced its largest acquisition to date, purchasing chat software developer Slack for over $27 billion in a combination of cash and stock. This deal positions Salesforce to further compete with Microsoft in the enterprise software market, expanding its portfolio of applications and seeking new growth areas. The acquisition is a significant move in CEO Marc Benioff's multiyear acquisition strategy, following previous large deals like Tableau and MuleSoft.

title: Judge throws out Trump rules limiting skilled-worker visas
summary: A federal judge in California has struck down two Trump administration rules that aimed to significantly reduce the number of H-1B visas issued to skilled foreign workers. The judge ruled that the government failed to follow proper transparency procedures and that its argument of an emergency response to COVID-19 job losses was unconvincing. This decision is seen as a significant relief for companies and current H-1B visa holders.

title: CNH Industrial, Accenture and Microsoft Collaborate to Develop Connected Industrial Vehicles
summary: CNH Industrial, Accenture, and Microsoft have entered a five-year agreement to enhance CNH Industrial's digital capabilities and develop smart connected products and services. The collaboration involves creating a global network of digital hubs to design and manage digital services for connected vehicles, focusing on areas like computer-aided farming, predictive maintenance, and sustainable transportation. This initiative aims to drive revenue growth for CNH Industrial by transitioning from a product-sales-based model to one that includes digital-driven services.

title: What Salesforce’s $27.7 Billion Acquisition of Slack Means for the Workplace
summary: Salesforce announced its acquisition of Slack for $27.7 billion, making it Salesforce's largest purchase and one of the biggest acquisitions of 2020. Slack will become the interface for Salesforce’s software, integrating with Salesforce Customer 360 and opening Salesforce to a wider business audience. This deal also intensifies competition with Microsoft, which offers Microsoft Teams.

title: Slack sold to business software giant for $27.7bn
summary: Salesforce has agreed to acquire workplace messaging app Slack for $27.7 billion (£20bn) in a major tech merger driven by the increased focus on remote work during the pandemic. This acquisition positions Salesforce to expand its software offerings and intensify its rivalry with Microsoft, which had previously launched a competing product, Microsoft Teams, that outpaced Slack in user numbers. The deal is seen as strategic for Slack, providing it with resources to better compete against dominant tech giants like Microsoft, especially after Slack's previous struggles against Teams.

title: Chegg Appoints Sarah Bond to Board of Directors
summary: Chegg, Inc. has announced the appointment of Sarah Bond, Corporate Vice President of Gaming Ecosystem at Microsoft, to its Board of Directors, effective December 2, 2020. Bond brings extensive experience in building technology partnerships and driving company growth, particularly with subscription-based services like Xbox Game Pass. Her expertise is expected to help Chegg further its student-first mission and adapt to evolving educational models.

title: Investing in the Future of Water
summary: Ecolab has joined the Global Water Impact Fund, a $100 million technology venture fund, alongside partners like Microsoft and Temasek Holdings. The fund aims to invest in early-stage companies developing innovative water conservation technologies for industrial applications. This initiative supports Ecolab's goal to help customers save 300 billion gallons of water by 2030 and address the looming global freshwater shortage.

title: Amazon's AWS To Leverage Israeli-Made AI Processors By Habana Labs
summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) announced it will use Israeli AI processor developer Habana Labs' Gaudi accelerators. This move aims to reduce the cost of training AI datasets and lower operating expenses for customers, offering up to 40% better price-performance than current GPU-based EC2 instances for machine learning workloads. This development is seen as a significant challenge to Nvidia's dominance in the AI processing market.

title: This chart shows how the Salesforce acquisition of Slack for $27.7 billion stacks up against tech's largest deals ever
summary: Salesforce announced its intent to acquire Slack for $27.7 billion, making it one of the largest tech acquisitions in history, surpassing Microsoft's LinkedIn purchase. This move highlights Salesforce's strategy to expand its enterprise software offerings and compete directly with Microsoft Teams. The article provides a detailed list of the 28 most expensive tech acquisitions, showcasing how Salesforce's Slack deal compares to other major transactions, from Apple's Beats acquisition to Dell's purchase of EMC.

title: A Microsoft custom data type for efficient inference
summary: Microsoft introduces MSFP, a new custom data type optimized for efficient deep neural network (DNN) inference, which is crucial for AI features in products like Bing and Office 365. MSFP provides higher accuracy with fewer bits per value than traditional floating-point formats, striking a better balance between cost and accuracy for AI models. This technology is being leveraged through Project Brainwave, using FPGAs and custom silicon, to deliver large-scale, real-time DNN inference in the cloud.

title: Hewlett Packard Enterprise becomes latest tech firm to leave Silicon Valley
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) is relocating its headquarters from San Jose, California, to Houston, Texas, following a trend of tech companies moving out of Silicon Valley. This move, despite HPE's historical roots in Palo Alto, is driven by factors like California's high cost of living and the rise of remote work during the pandemic. The company also reported strong quarterly revenues that topped analyst predictions, suggesting businesses are upgrading data-center hardware.

title: Microsoft apologises for feature criticised as workplace surveillance
summary: Microsoft has apologized for its "productivity score" feature after criticism that it amounted to workplace surveillance. The company will now remove individual user names from the service, ensuring that data is only aggregated at the organizational level to protect employee privacy. This change aims to clarify that the feature assesses organizational, not individual, productivity.

title: Salesforce to buy workplace app Slack in $27.7 bln deal
summary: Salesforce announced its agreement to acquire workplace messaging app Slack for $27.7 billion, marking its largest-ever acquisition. This deal aims to enhance Salesforce's enterprise offerings, enable it to deepen its presence in collaboration and communication tools, and intensify its rivalry with Microsoft in the remote working solutions market. Despite a premium offer for Slack shareholders, both companies' stocks saw declines following the announcement.

title: Chegg Appoints Sarah Bond to Board of Directors
summary: Chegg, Inc. has appointed Sarah Bond, Corporate Vice President of Gaming Ecosystem at Microsoft, to its Board of Directors, effective December 2, 2020. Bond brings extensive experience in subscription-based services and building online communities, having been instrumental in scaling Xbox Game Pass. Both Chegg's CEO and Bond expressed enthusiasm for her contributions, highlighting her alignment with Chegg's student-first mission and expertise in rapidly evolving technology sectors.

title: Tech giant Hewlett Packard Enterprise moving Silicon Valley headquarters from San Jose to Houston
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise is moving its headquarters from San Jose, California, to Houston, Texas, despite maintaining offices in San Jose. This move is part of a broader trend of companies leaving Silicon Valley, often citing high costs of living and taxes, though experts like Dilawar Syed believe Silicon Valley will remain a key place for innovation. Ahmad Thomas of the Silicon Valley Leadership Group sees this as a "wake-up call" for California to improve its tax competitiveness and infrastructure.

title: Labster – Science Labs in Virtual Reality
summary: Labster, a Danish startup, has raised $150.5 million in funding to develop virtual reality science lab simulations for educational institutions. The company has seen a significant increase in usage during the pandemic and has partnered with over 1,000 universities and 3,000 high schools globally. Labster's approach provides a cost-effective alternative to physical labs, aiming to enhance learning experiences, especially for disadvantaged students, and is conducting research to validate the efficacy of VR in education.

title: DXC Technology and Microsoft Collaborate to Power Modern Workplace Experience
summary: DXC Technology and Microsoft have announced an expanded strategic collaboration to deliver an enhanced modern workplace experience through DXC MyWorkStyle. This solution, leveraging AI and machine learning, will provide personalized, intelligent, and secure tools for employees to work seamlessly from anywhere. DXC, a major provider of workplace services, will also implement the MyWorkStyle platform for its own employees globally.

title: Huggies launches biodegradable baby wipes in step towards plastic-free goal
summary: Huggies, owned by Kimberly-Clark, has introduced its first biodegradable baby wipes in the UK, aiming to eliminate plastics from its wipe range over the next five years. These new Huggies Pure Biodegradable wipes are made from 100% natural fibers and are designed to break down in landfill conditions within 15 days, contributing to a significant reduction in plastic usage. This initiative follows pressure from consumers and media to address the environmental impact of wet wipes, aligning with Huggies' "Tiniest Footprint" Mission and WRAP’s UK Plastic Pact.

title: Microsoft and NSDC join hands for the Imagine Cup 2021 in India
summary: Microsoft India and the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) have partnered for the India edition of the Microsoft Imagine Cup 2021, an annual innovation challenge for students. This virtual competition aims to empower students to use AI and other technologies to address critical social and sustainability issues across categories like Earth, Education, Health, and Lifestyle. Winners will receive significant prize money and mentorship opportunities, including with Microsoft's CEO Satya Nadella.

title: A culture of innovation is key to exploring new frontiers of economic recovery and resilience
summary: This article emphasizes that a culture of innovation is crucial for economic recovery and resilience, especially in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic. It highlights a study conducted with IDC Asia Pacific, which found that organizations fostering continuous innovation through people, data, processes, and technology are better positioned for long-term success. The piece also provides examples of Indian companies leveraging digital transformation and stresses the importance of upskilling the workforce and embedding innovation as a core corporate value.

title: C3 AI Supply Network Risk
summary: C3 AI Supply Network Risk is a solution designed to empower enterprises in building resilient and agile supply networks. It offers real-time visibility, predictive agents, and AI-driven optimization to anticipate disruptions and respond effectively. The application unifies various enterprise and external data sources, applying advanced AI to detect risks and recommend actions for faster, smarter, and more strategic decisions.

title: Deutsche Bank to Move ‘Heart’ of IT Systems Into Google’s Cloud
summary: Deutsche Bank AG has finalized a cloud computing agreement with Alphabet Inc.'s Google to migrate most of its data onto Google servers, aiming to modernize its IT systems and cut costs. This long-term contract is expected to yield a cumulative return on investment of 1 billion euros for Deutsche Bank and marks a significant step for Google into the European banking cloud market. The partnership also includes joint development of new financial products, with both companies planning to sell some of this technology as white-label products.

title: 3 Best Practices for Using Third-Party B2B Buyer Intent Data in ABM
summary: This article outlines three best practices for utilizing third-party B2B buyer intent data in Account-Based Marketing (ABM) campaigns. It emphasizes the importance of researching multiple data sources, using intent data to inform content decisions, and preparing for privacy and regulatory concerns. The goal is to help software providers identify and engage prospective buyers more effectively.

title: Danielle Ecuyer reveals where she would invest $10k
summary: Danielle Ecuyer, a finance expert, discusses two hypothetical investment portfolios for $10,000, catering to different risk appetites. She details her investment strategy changes during the volatile year of 2020, including sales and purchases in response to the pandemic and economic stimulus, emphasizing capital preservation and adaptation. Ecuyer also highlights current market conditions, such as speculative retail investment and potential shifts from growth to cyclical stocks due to inflation.

title: 2021 ESG Trends to Watch
summary: This article outlines five key ESG trends for 2021, emphasizing the increasing maturity of ESG investing beyond hype and skepticism. It highlights the growing challenges for investors to align with Paris Agreement goals due to shrinking eligible opportunities, the surge in corporate ESG disclosures driven by new regulations, and the urgent need for investors to address systemic risks like social inequality and biodiversity loss, exacerbated by events like COVID-19. The article provides an overview of various aspects, including climate reality and financial implications for investors, the evolving understanding of ESG's pecuniary benefits, the impending biodiversity crisis, the "data deluge" of ESG reporting requirements, and investors' creative approaches to tackle social inequalities, including the rise of social bonds.

title: Exploitation of Windows RDP Vulnerability CVE-2019-0708 (BlueKeep)
summary: This article details the exploitation of the Windows RDP vulnerability CVE-2019-0708, known as "BlueKeep," to achieve remote code execution (RCE) with system privileges. It explains how attackers can combine Refresh Rect PDU and RDPDR Client Name Request PDU to control execution flow and inject shellcode. The authors also highlight how Palo Alto Networks' products, including Next-Generation Firewall and Cortex XDR, protect customers from this vulnerability.

title: Popular Android apps like Grindr, OkCupid, and others vulnerable to major security flaw: Check Point
summary: A security flaw, CVE-2020-8913, rooted in Google's Play Core Library, continues to affect popular Android apps like Grindr, Bumble, Cisco Teams, and OkCupid, despite Google having issued a fix in April 2020. This vulnerability allows cybercriminals to inject and execute malicious code, potentially leading to the theft of sensitive user data, including login and financial details. Developers of the affected apps still need to implement the updated Play Core library to fully eliminate the threat, putting millions of users at risk.

title: Juniper Acquires Apstra for Scaleable Automation
summary: Juniper Networks announced its intent to acquire Apstra, a pioneer in intent-based networking (IBN) and intent-based analytics (IBA). This acquisition aims to boost Juniper's presence in multi-cloud networking and reinforce its mission to become a software-based solutions provider, challenging rivals like Cisco. The deal's financial terms were undisclosed, but it is expected to be accretive to revenue and earnings by early 2022.

title: 3 unique success stories—building resilience into the supply chain
summary: This article highlights three organizations that successfully leveraged Microsoft Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management to build resilience and agility into their operations, especially in response to the challenges posed by the 2020 supply chain shock. Wahl Clipper Corporation, JB Hi-Fi Group, and Invitalia each demonstrate how modern cloud solutions can dramatically shorten deployment times and enable faster decision-making, improved data harmonization, and efficient logistics management. The case studies emphasize the versatility, scalability, and rapid time-to-value offered by intelligent cloud-based solutions in navigating disruptions and adapting to changing business needs.

title: SAP Hires New Chief Design Officer
summary: SAP announced that Benedikt Lehnert will join the company as chief design officer, effective January 1, 2021. Lehnert, previously from Microsoft, will work with Alexander Lingg to define one design system and intensify SAP's focus on consumer needs in software application design. This move signifies SAP's reintroduction of the chief design officer role to ensure a consistent user experience across its Intelligent Enterprise solution portfolio.

title: CodeSignal raises $25M for its developer assessment platform
summary: CodeSignal, a startup providing a coding platform for developer recruitment, announced it has raised $25 million in a funding round led by Menlo Ventures and joined by Capital One Financial Corp.'s venture capital arm. The platform helps companies assess candidates' programming expertise through pre-packaged coding tasks and automated scoring, aiming to reduce manual assessment work. CodeSignal plans to use the new funding to accelerate hiring and sales, expanding into more verticals, after experiencing 350% revenue growth in the past year.

title: Audio Quick Take: Aon’s Rakesh Inamdar on Being a Digital Leader
summary: This HBR Audio Quick Take features Rakesh Inamdar from Aon discussing how the company has achieved digital leadership through strategic technology investments in areas like big data analytics, elastic compute, and AI. Aon's focus on a resilient, scalable, and globally reachable digital infrastructure, including partnerships with companies like Equinix, allowed them to maintain operations efficiently, even during the COVID-19 pandemic. Looking ahead, Aon plans further investments in AI, Machine Learning, and 5G to drive future business insights and transform network connectivity.

title: Uber sells ATG self-driving business to Aurora at $4 billion
summary: Uber Technologies Inc is selling its autonomous driving unit, Uber Advanced Technologies Group (ATG), to self-driving car startup Aurora in an equity deal valued at $4 billion. Uber will also invest $400 million in Aurora, giving it approximately 26% ownership, with the aim to accelerate Uber's path to profitability by the end of 2021. This sale marks a significant drop in ATG's valuation from its previous $7.25 billion.

title: BoldData releases Top 100 Toy and Gaming Companies by revenue
summary: BoldData has released a list of the top 100 toy and gaming companies by revenue, highlighting the significant shift from traditional toys to digital gaming. The report shows US companies like Hasbro and Mattel leading the traditional toy market, while Japan and the US dominate the digital gaming industry, with Nintendo topping the list. Europe also features prominently, particularly for traditional toy manufacturers.

title: Banks look at ‘explainable’ AI systems to boost consumer trust
summary: Financial institutions are investing in "explainable" artificial intelligence (AI) to address concerns about algorithmic bias and lack of transparency in automated decision-making. This technology aims to make AI decisions more traceable and understandable for auditors, regulators, and consumers, helping to build trust and mitigate issues like discrimination in loan denials. While explainable AI offers solutions to the "black box" problem, experts caution that poorly structured data can still lead to skewed outcomes, emphasizing the need for continuous fine-tuning and good governance.

title: Exclusive: AvePoint CEO Talks Microsoft Relationship, User Growth, SPAC Deal
summary: AvePoint CEO TJ Jiang discussed the company's decision to go public via a SPAC merger with Apex Technology Acquisition Corporation, valuing the company at $2 billion. He highlighted AvePoint's 19-year relationship with Microsoft, its role as a top independent software vendor, and its strong user growth from 7 million to an ambitious goal of 50 million active users. Jiang also emphasized the company's financial discipline, high growth, and shift towards recurring revenue through subscription services.

title: Over 200 million users rely on SharePoint as Microsoft is again recognized as a Leader in the 2020 Gartner Content Services Platforms Magic Quadrant Report
summary: Microsoft's SharePoint has reached over 200 million monthly active users, demonstrating significant growth and impact across Microsoft 365. For the fourth consecutive year, Gartner has recognized Microsoft as a Leader in the Content Services Platforms Magic Quadrant for 2020, highlighting its innovation in content collaboration and protection powered by AI. The article details how SharePoint underpins various Microsoft 365 services and platforms, supporting leading companies and announcing continued investment in its architecture for future innovations.

title: Best Buy wants 1 in 3 new corporate hires to be people of color
summary: Best Buy announced a plan to have people of color fill one-third of its new corporate jobs over the next five years, aligning with similar diversity targets set by other major companies. This initiative is part of a broader $44 million diversity push, which also includes financial support for students attending Historically Black Colleges and Universities and the establishment of "Teen Tech Centers" in underserved communities. Other companies like Google, Microsoft, Wells Fargo, and Starbucks have also committed to increasing racial diversity within their leadership and workforce by 2025.

title: Gartner’s Magic Quadrant for Cloud Database Management Systems
summary: Gartner's Magic Quadrant for Cloud Database Management Systems highlights 16 leading vendors in the rapidly growing cloud DBMS market, which is projected to account for 50 percent of the total DBMS market by 2023. The report categorizes vendors into Leaders, Challengers, Visionaries, and Niche Players based on their ability to execute and completeness of vision. Key players like AWS, Microsoft, Oracle, and Google are identified as leaders, with detailed strengths and weaknesses provided for each featured vendor.

title: Adobe Flash Player Receives Final Software Update As It Walks Death Row
summary: Adobe has released its final software update for Flash Player, marking the end of its support after December 31, 2020. All Flash content will be blocked from running starting January 12, 2021, and Adobe strongly recommends users uninstall the player due to its long history of security vulnerabilities. This phase-out comes over a decade after Steve Jobs famously criticized Flash for its proprietary nature, security flaws, and performance issues.

title: Nature Conservancy Hooked Corporate America on an Empty Climate Solution
summary: The Nature Conservancy, the world's largest environmental group, is accused of selling "meaningless" carbon offsets to major corporations like JPMorgan, Disney, and BlackRock. These offsets are based on preserving forestland that was never actually threatened with deforestation. Critics argue that this practice allows companies to claim significant emissions reductions without making genuine changes to their operations, undermining efforts to combat climate change.

title: How Microsoft designed a campus with the evolution of work in mind
summary: Microsoft's new 46,000 square meter campus in Herzliya, Israel, was designed with the future of work in mind, emphasizing sustainability, dynamic urban environments, and flexible, inclusive workspaces. The campus achieved LEED V4 Building Design and Construction Gold certification, utilizing atmospheric generators for water and photovoltaic cells for energy. Its innovative design, including team-based "neighborhoods" and extensive amenities, aims to create a lifestyle experience rather than just an office, prioritizing employee well-being, accessibility, and adaptability for evolving work needs.

title: Oracle reports slow revenue growth as licensing and hardware businesses decline
summary: Oracle reported fiscal second-quarter earnings that beat analysts' expectations, with adjusted earnings of $1.06 per share on revenue of $9.80 billion, despite shares initially falling before recovering. While cloud services saw increased demand, the company's traditional licensing and hardware businesses experienced declines. Oracle's deal to become a cloud provider for TikTok in the U.S. is still pending finalization.

title: The dark reality behind Slack’s billion-dollar sale to Salesforce
summary: The article discusses Slack's acquisition by Salesforce for $27.7 billion, framing it as a "defensive" move rather than a success story. It argues that Slack, despite its innovative product, was unable to compete against Microsoft's bundling of Teams, highlighting a broader issue of tech giants stifling smaller innovators through monopolistic practices. The author suggests that this trend threatens consumer choice and calls for a rebalancing of the playing field against unchecked corporate power.

title: 8x8: Verma Out as CEO, Sipes In
summary: 8x8 announced the departure of CEO Vik Verma and the appointment of former RingCentral COO Dave Sipes as his replacement. This leadership change comes as UCaaS providers struggle against competitors like Zoom and Microsoft, with analysts offering mixed but generally positive views on Sipes's ability to navigate 8x8 in a competitive market.

title: Gartner dishes out an HCI MQ Christmas surprise
summary: Gartner has significantly changed the criteria for its Hyperconverged Infrastructure (HCI) Magic Quadrant (MQ) for 2020, focusing only on HCI software players. This narrowed definition led to the exclusion of major vendors like Cisco, Dell EMC, HPE, Huawei, and Red Hat, which previously offered integrated HCI systems. Consequently, Nutanix and VMware remain as leaders, Microsoft is the sole visionary, and other vendors like Pivot3, Scale Computing, StorMagic, and Starwind are positioned as niche players.

title: Werner's new cloud-based transportation management system
summary: Werner Enterprises, a large freight carrier, is transitioning to a cloud-first technology strategy by implementing a new cloud-based transportation management system (TMS) called MasterMind from startup Mastery Logistics Systems. This move aims to accelerate business growth, optimize IT resources, and enhance tools for drivers and customers. Werner has also made a minority equity investment in Mastery Logistics Systems and is providing strategic advisement for product development.

title: What’s Changed: 2020 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Metadata Management Solutions
summary: This article reviews the 2020 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Metadata Management Solutions, highlighting significant changes and vendor movements. It details key players like Informatica, IBM, Collibra, and others, analyzing their strengths and positioning within the market. The report also introduces new entrants and shifts in vendor categories based on Gartner's evaluation criteria.

title: 3M manufacturing plant uses data analytics to increase efficiency and cost savings with Azure SQL Edge
summary: 3M partnered with Microsoft to implement Azure SQL Edge at one of its US manufacturing plants to increase efficiency and achieve cost savings. By integrating data streams from two production lines, correlating them, and running analytics and machine learning locally, 3M can now predict anomalies and reduce manufacturing downtime. This solution addresses limited network connectivity and disparate data sources, positioning 3M for Industry 4.0.

title: Electronic Arts (EA) Expands VR Game Portfolio With New Launch
summary: Electronic Arts (EA), through its studio Respawn Entertainment, has released "Medal of Honor: Above and Beyond," a new virtual reality (VR) title in partnership with Facebook Reality Labs’ Oculus Studios. This launch boosts EA's VR game portfolio and comes as the company benefits from increased demand for video games. Despite strong competition from companies like Take Two Interactive and Activision Blizzard, EA continues to expand its offerings with new titles across various platforms to attract gamers.

title: Microsoft Teams Statistics
summary: This article compiles various statistics about Microsoft Teams, highlighting its significant growth in adoption and usage, especially during 2020. It covers daily active users, geographical spread, education sector usage, app downloads, community engagement, video and meeting data, business case benefits, employee management improvements, and Microsoft's related revenue. The data underscores Teams' rapid expansion and its impact across different sectors and company operations.

title: Threat Brief: SolarStorm and SUNBURST Customer Coverage
summary: This threat brief details the SolarStorm campaign, also known as UNC2452, which utilizes the SUNBURST backdoor via a supply chain attack on SolarWinds Orion Platform. It outlines the attack's nature, indicators of compromise (IOCs) for SUNBURST and TEARDROP malware, and how Palo Alto Networks products protect customers. The article emphasizes the importance of identifying affected systems and provides resources for assessment and mitigation.

title: Electronic Arts outbids Take-Two with $1.2 billion deal for Codemasters
summary: Electronic Arts (EA) has agreed to acquire Codemasters for $1.2 billion, outbidding an earlier offer from Take-Two Interactive Software. The deal, which offers Codemasters' shareholders 604 pence per share, is considered superior to Take-Two's previous offer of 485 pence per share and is expected to close in the first quarter of 2021. This acquisition will strengthen EA's position in racing games and is anticipated to boost its net bookings and profitability.

title: Microsoft and Warner Bros. Pictures Assemble All-Star Team in LeBron James, Bugs Bunny and Xbox to Celebrate Gaming and Coding Education Inspired By The Upcoming Animated, Live-Action Adventure 'Space Jam: A New Legacy'
summary: Microsoft and Warner Bros. are launching a partnership with LeBron James, Bugs Bunny, and Xbox to promote coding education, inspired by the upcoming movie 'Space Jam: A New Legacy'. This initiative includes a fan contest to design an Xbox arcade-style video game, free coding workshops, and Microsoft Learn lessons focusing on game design and real-time decision-making using player stats. These efforts align with Microsoft's broader goal to help 25 million people acquire new digital skills.

title: The leading enterprise cybersecurity companies 2021
summary: IoT Analytics identified Cisco, Microsoft, and Palo Alto Networks as the most popular enterprise cybersecurity companies in 2021 through a 120-page report analyzing 99 companies. The research highlights a sharp increase in cyberattacks during 2020, emphasizing the importance of choosing effective cybersecurity solutions. Key trends include the growing adoption of cloud-based and AI/ML-based security solutions, with surveyed companies averaging only 12 out of 29 possible cybersecurity solutions deployed.

title: Acquisition of Oi's mobile ops neutral to TIM, Telefonica Brasil and America Movil
summary: Fitch Ratings believes the proposed acquisition of Oi S.A.'s mobile operations by a consortium of TIM S.A., Telefonica Brasil S.A., and America Movil will not negatively impact the credit quality of the buyers. The companies' strong financial profiles and robust balance sheets will allow them to absorb the BRL16.5 billion (USD3.2 billion) acquisition. The deal, if approved, is expected to improve market share, scale, and synergies for the acquiring companies in the Brazilian telecommunications sector.

title: Coca-Cola Bottling Company United dispenses streamlined order management with RPA in Microsoft Power Automate
summary: Coca-Cola Bottling Company United implemented robotic process automation (RPA) using Microsoft Power Automate to streamline order and invoicing processes for its Freestyle vending machines. This solution, developed with Happiest Minds, automates an 11-step manual process, freeing up CRM agents and allowing the company to scale its Freestyle initiative more effectively. The RPA solution, dubbed "Asa," handles order entry, PO creation, supplier interaction, invoice processing, and data storage, significantly reducing labor costs and potential errors.

title: Amazon urges judge to set aside $10 billion cloud contract award to Microsoft
summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) has urged a U.S. judge to invalidate the Pentagon's $10 billion JEDI cloud computing contract award to Microsoft, alleging systematic bias and undue influence from President Trump. Amazon contends that a recent re-evaluation found AWS to be the lowest-priced bid by tens of millions of dollars, yet the contract remained with Microsoft, a decision Amazon calls "flawed and politically corrupted." A temporary halt on the deal remains in place while motions to dismiss Amazon's amended complaint are considered.

title: The Starbucks app in Microsoft Teams—a new way to show appreciation for your colleagues this holiday season and beyond
summary: Microsoft has introduced a new Starbucks app within Microsoft Teams, allowing users in the US and Canada to send personalized Starbucks eGifts directly through chat. This feature is designed to help colleagues show appreciation, especially while working remotely, and is part of a long-term partnership between Starbucks and Microsoft. Additionally, Starbucks has provided new holiday-themed Team backgrounds to enhance virtual celebrations.

title: Many Canadian employers say they won’t continue work-from-home flexibility after pandemic
summary: A significant number of Canadian employers do not plan to maintain flexible work-from-home policies once the pandemic ends, creating a potential disconnect with employee expectations. Studies show a strong preference for remote or flexible work, particularly among younger employees, which could lead to a wave of job market transitions as workers seek opportunities aligning with their new lifestyle preferences. This situation presents a challenge for employers, especially smaller organizations, in attracting and retaining talent, underscoring the need for open dialogue and adaptation to evolving employee demands.

title: $286M Of SolarWinds Stock Sold Before CEO, Hack Disclosures
summary: SolarWinds majority owners Silver Lake and Thoma Bravo sold $286 million of stock just before the company announced a new CEO and disclosed a cyberattack. The private equity firms disposed of more than 13 million SolarWinds stock shares at $21.97 per share on December 7, two days before the IT infrastructure management firm announced its next CEO and four days before disclosing a highly sophisticated supply chain attack. The firms claim they were unaware of the cyberattack at the time of the sale, but did not answer questions about their knowledge of the new CEO selection.

title: SUPERNOVA: A Novel .NET Webshell, an Analysis
summary: This article analyzes SUPERNOVA, a novel .NET webshell identified in the SolarWinds supply chain attack. It highlights SUPERNOVA's sophisticated in-memory execution and dynamic compilation capabilities, which make it difficult to detect with traditional endpoint security. The authors detail how the webshell operates as an interactive .NET runtime API, allowing attackers to deploy arbitrary C# code.

title: Apple Inc. stock rises Thursday, still underperforms market
summary: Apple Inc. (AAPL) stock increased by 0.70% on Thursday to $128.70, during a generally favorable trading session for the market where the NASDAQ Composite Index and Dow Jones Industrial Average also rose. Despite this, Apple's stock closed below its 52-week high but outperformed some competitors like Microsoft and Alphabet. Trading volume was lower than its 50-day average.

title: Cloud recasts global data center switch market
summary: The global data center switch market is being reshaped by cloud providers and enterprise cloud makers, leading to a decline in traditional networking gear sales. White box switches, favored by large-scale cloud environments, saw significant growth while established vendors like Arista Networks, Cisco, and Juniper Networks experienced revenue drops. This shift demands that vendors reconfigure their products and software to be cloud-focused, addressing enterprise needs for independent management software and hybrid environments.

title: EA, Take-Two Involved in Billion-Dollar Bidding War Over Racing Game Maker
summary: Electronic Arts (EA) has outbid Take-Two Interactive Software (TTWO) for Codemasters, a British video game developer known for its racing games, raising its offer to $1.2 billion after Take-Two's initial $971 million pact. Analysts view Codemasters as a valuable acquisition due to its solid IP, profitability, and growth opportunities in live services and mobile gaming, despite some concerns about potential overvaluation and EA's history with racing franchises. The bidding war highlights the ongoing consolidation trend in the video game industry, driven by the pursuit of scale, the pandemic-induced gaming boom, and the importance of owning valuable intellectual property.

title: Why COVID-19 fuels desktop virtualization trends
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic significantly accelerated the adoption of desktop virtualization (VDI) as organizations shifted to work-from-home models. VDI offers benefits like centralized management, cost-effectiveness through immediate updates, and flexibility, allowing users to access resources from any device. However, VDI also presents challenges such as the need for significant data center investment, potential bandwidth contention, and the risk of a single point of failure.

title: Verizon debuts On Site LTE to let enterprises build on-prem 4G networks
summary: Verizon has introduced On Site LTE, a new hardware-software bundle enabling enterprises to create miniature 4G networks on their premises. This solution provides a robust wireless connectivity alternative to Wi-Fi for industrial IoT devices and other demanding applications. Alongside On Site LTE, Verizon also launched IoT Managed Services to assist companies lacking in-house technical expertise with planning and deploying IoT projects.

title: Moore From L.A.: What Fashion Brands Can Learn From Mattel and Toys
summary: Mattel's president and COO, Richard Dickson, discusses how the company has grown, particularly with Barbie and Hot Wheels, by connecting products to pop culture and expanding collaborations. He highlights the success of limited-edition co-branded products through Mattel Creations and suggests that fashion brands can learn from Mattel's approach to toys as an ongoing business opportunity rather than just seasonal accessories. Dickson also touches on the importance of storytelling, digital content, and balancing nostalgia with newness in brand strategy.

title: Element AI sold for $230-million as founders saw value mostly wiped out, document reveals
summary: Montreal startup Element AI Inc. was sold to ServiceNow Inc. for US$230-million, a deal that saw the value of common shares held by founders and many employees largely wiped out due to the company's financial struggles and inability to meet product development goals. While institutional shareholders are expected to recoup investments, the sale highlights the challenges faced by the highly hyped AI firm despite significant venture capital and government funding. The transaction involves ServiceNow retaining Element AI's research scientists and patents, effectively abandoning its business.

title: Salesforce’s Marc Benioff is betting $28 billion on Bret Taylor. So who is he?
summary: The article profiles Bret Taylor, Salesforce's Chief Operating Officer and the architect behind its $27.7 billion acquisition of Slack. It highlights Taylor's impressive career trajectory, including his work at Google and Facebook, and his entrepreneurial success with FriendFeed and Quip. The piece also delves into speculation about Taylor potentially succeeding co-founder Marc Benioff as CEO, emphasizing his growing influence and the high regard in which he is held within the tech industry.

title: Tesla's Elon Musk asks about converting "large transactions" to bitcoin
summary: Elon Musk, CEO of Tesla, inquired on Twitter about the feasibility of converting significant portions of Tesla's balance sheet into Bitcoin. This query came in response to MicroStrategy CEO Michael Saylor's suggestion that such a move could greatly benefit Tesla shareholders, leading to an exchange where Saylor offered to share his experience with large Bitcoin purchases. The discussion coincided with Bitcoin's recent surge past $20,000 and Tesla's upcoming entry into the S&P 500 index.

title: Fidelity MSCI Information Technology Index ETF FTEC
summary: This article provides an overview of the Fidelity MSCI Information Technology Index ETF (FTEC), detailing its current price, key metrics, and how to purchase it on eToro. The ETF aims to replicate the performance of the MSCI USA IMI Information Technology Index, focusing primarily on US-based IT companies like Apple, Microsoft, and NVIDIA. It highlights the ETF's investment strategy, top holdings, and historical performance data.

title: The cloud polyglot
summary: The article introduces the concept of a "cloud polyglot," referring to individuals capable of managing multiple cloud infrastructures, both on-premises and hyperscalers. It highlights the challenges of user experience fragmentation across various cloud platforms despite their similar underlying services. The author proposes NetApp ONTAP data management software and NetApp Cloud Manager as a potential solution to achieve a unified experience for managing storage and data in hybrid, multicloud environments.

title: Cognizant (CTSH) Boosts Data Analytics With Inawisdom Buyout
summary: Cognizant (CTSH) has acquired Inawisdom, a UK-based consultancy specializing in AI, machine learning, and data analytics. This acquisition enhances Cognizant's digital capabilities, particularly in cloud-native AI-driven data analytics and machine learning solutions, leveraging Amazon Web Services. It is part of Cognizant's broader strategy of nine acquisitions in 2020, aimed at strengthening its presence in cloud transformation, digital engineering, and IoT, contributing to significant growth in bookings and revenue.

title: 3 critical employee experience technologies for the 'new normal'
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic has accelerated the adoption of technology in HR to support employee experience. This article highlights three key technological advancements: conversational AI for streamlined talent sourcing, AI for boosting internal talent mobility, and employee well-being technology to address mental and emotional health. These technologies help companies adapt to a distributed workforce, improve hiring efficiency, foster career development, and prioritize employee health.

title: SolarStorm Supply Chain Attack Timeline
summary: This article details the SolarStorm supply chain attack, which affected SolarWinds Orion software and numerous organizations globally. It provides a timeline of the attack, from infrastructure setup in August 2019 to the discovery and response in December 2020, and highlights various tools and techniques used by the attackers, including malicious updates and SAML token forging. The article also discusses Palo Alto Networks' successful prevention of an attempted SolarStorm attack and outlines past software supply chain compromises, emphasizing the ongoing threat these attacks pose.

title: Coca-Cola UNITED manages rapid growth with Microsoft Power Platform
summary: Coca-Cola UNITED successfully leveraged Microsoft Power Platform to manage rapid growth, expanding operations and sales significantly. The low-code platform enabled quick development of applications for order processing and event management, streamlining operations and improving customer satisfaction. This adoption allowed Coca-Cola UNITED to move away from time-consuming custom coding and innovate faster.

title: NetApp’s Israeli VPs leading the company’s cloud service forward
summary: Roy Alon and Assaf Levy, who joined NetApp after their startup Onaro was acquired 13 years ago, are now jointly managing NetApp's cloud activity from Israel. They have significantly grown NetApp's cloud offering, which generated $216 million in the past year, and have led acquisitions of six startups, including two Israeli companies. They discuss the growth of NetApp's cloud services, the move of data centers to the cloud, and the importance of data management and security in their acquisition strategy.

title: Machine Translation Market 2020-2024 | The Globalization Of Business to Boost Market Growth and Post a CAGR of 19% | Technavio
summary: The machine translation market is projected to grow by USD 971.87 million between 2020 and 2024, at a CAGR of 19%, driven primarily by the globalization of business. While this trend creates significant opportunities, data privacy and security risks in online translation services pose challenges for market participants. The report identifies key vendors, segmentation by application and geography, and highlights the increasing localization of video content as a key driver.

title: WEBL ETF Continues Its Climb, Rises Over 20% Past Month
summary: The Direxion Daily Dow Jones Internet Bull 3X Shares (WEBL) ETF has seen a significant rise, climbing over 20% in the past month, driven by increased internet usage due to coronavirus social distancing measures. The article highlights the fund's strong performance, trading above its 50-day and 200-day moving averages, and discusses how recent stimulus packages are further supporting internet access for lower-income Americans, which could continue to benefit internet-related investments.

title: Russians Are Believed to Have Used Microsoft Resellers in Cyberattacks (Published 2020)
summary: New evidence suggests that Russian hackers, responsible for the SolarWinds attack, also utilized companies selling software on Microsoft's behalf to compromise customers' Office 365 accounts. These resellers, entrusted with client software, became vulnerable points in the supply chain, similar to the SolarWinds compromise. Cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike notably experienced an unsuccessful attack through a Microsoft reseller.

title: Understanding the Video Gaming and Esports Landscape
summary: This article provides a curated list of key resources for investors to understand the video gaming and esports industries. It highlights important reports and articles from Newzoo, Matthew Ball, Roundhill, Citi, YouGov, Nielsen, and Forbes, emphasizing themes like global market trends, the metaverse, livestreaming, cloud gaming, and esports valuations. The contributing author offers key takeaways from each recommended resource, providing insights into the evolving landscape of these industries.

title: Honor partners Microsoft for OS
summary: Honor, newly independent from Huawei, has inked a global cooperation agreement with Microsoft to use Windows 10 as the official operating system for its laptops. This partnership is seen as a positive sign for Honor's future supply chain solutions, potentially leading to collaborations with other US tech giants like Qualcomm. The new Honor MagicBook series, featuring Windows 10, will launch in China in January 2021, with an international debut of the MagicBook Pro also in January.

title: Zoom's Eric Yuan became one of the world's richest people in 2020 as Covid sent people rushing to meet on video
summary: Zoom CEO Eric Yuan saw his net worth skyrocket in 2020, making him one of the world's 100 richest people, as the pandemic drove unprecedented demand for video conferencing. The company's revenue quadrupled and profit increased 90-fold, with its stock gaining over 450%. Despite facing privacy concerns and questions about connections to China, Zoom solidified its position as a dominant platform.

title: Intel shares rise after Third Point urges chipmaker to explore strategic alternatives as market share deteriorates
summary: Hedge fund Third Point, which recently acquired a significant stake in Intel, is urging the chipmaker's board to explore strategic alternatives due to deteriorating market share against rivals like TSMC, Samsung, and AMD. Third Point highlighted concerns about Intel's loss of manufacturing leadership and its impact on U.S. national security. Intel has stated it welcomes input from investors to enhance shareholder value.

title: Speaker Spotlight: "staying on top of trends involves being a gamer yourself" says Roundhill Investments' Mario Stefanidis
summary: Mario Stefanidis of Roundhill Investments discusses the intersection of finance and the games industry, emphasizing the importance of being an active gamer to understand evolving trends. He highlights how the COVID-19 pandemic accelerated growth in gaming and predicts future trends like cloud gaming expansion and new VR titles. Stefanidis also shares insights into Roundhill Investments' focus on thematic investing in digital media and entertainment.

title: Exclusive: Hedge fund Third Point urges Intel to explore deal options
summary: Activist hedge fund Third Point LLC, which has amassed a nearly $1 billion stake in Intel Corp, is urging the U.S. chipmaker to explore strategic alternatives, including whether it should keep chip design and production under one roof. Third Point CEO Daniel Loeb sent a letter to Intel Chairman Omar Ishrak, calling for immediate action to boost the company's position, address "human capital management issue," and consider divesting failed acquisitions. This push comes as Intel has lost market share to competitors like TSMC, Samsung, and AMD, and its stock has underperformed the Nasdaq Composite Index.

title: WisdomTree Computing Portfolio Has Investors on Cloud Nine
summary: Cloud computing is emerging as a premier disruptive technology, and advisors can leverage this trend for client portfolios using WisdomTree's new Disruptive Growth Model Portfolio. This portfolio targets structural growth themes, including the "MT SAAS" basket of tech companies like Microsoft and Amazon, which are seen as potential successors to FAANG stocks. The WisdomTree Cloud Computing ETF (WCLD), a top performer, is a core component, tracking an index of emerging cloud-based software companies.

title: Microsoft says its source code was accessed in SolarWinds hack
summary: Microsoft has revealed that the hacking group responsible for the SolarWinds compromise gained access to some of its source code, indicating a significant escalation in the attackers' ambition. While Microsoft stated that no production services or customer data were affected, experts caution that access to source code could provide hackers with a "blueprint" to exploit vulnerabilities in Microsoft products. The ongoing investigation aims to determine the extent of the access and whether it serves as reconnaissance for future attacks.

title: Adobe Officially Ends Support of Its Era-Defining Flash Player Today
summary: Adobe has officially ended support for its Flash Player on December 31, 2020, after more than two decades, with content blocking scheduled to begin on January 12, 2021. The decision, made in 2017, recommends users uninstall the software due to security concerns, though Flash Player was pivotal in evolving web content. The Internet Archive plans to preserve popular Flash animations, games, and videos using an emulator called Ruffle.

title: Covid-19 Supercharged 2020's Tech Winners. What About 2021?
summary: The pandemic significantly boosted tech companies like Zoom, Shopify, and Nvidia in 2020, as they capitalized on trends such as remote work, cloud computing, video gaming, and e-commerce. While these companies saw massive gains, the article questions whether these trends will continue to drive growth as the virus recedes in 2021. The shift to cloud computing, in particular, was accelerated by shelter-in-place orders, with Zoom becoming an essential tool for virtualized offices.

title: Microsoft Says Russian Hackers Viewed Some of Its Source Code (Published 2020)
summary: Microsoft confirmed that Russian hackers gained deeper access into its network than previously thought, managing to view some of its source code through an employee account. Although the hackers could not modify the code or access customer data and production services, the incident highlights the extensive nature of the Russian hack that also targeted various U.S. government agencies and private corporations. The investigation into the breach, which reportedly began in October 2019, is ongoing.
